Title: Nepal-Tibet floods: Latest developments in deadly disaster
Article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal: More than 2,400 people are missing and at least 584 have been killed after a devastating, tsunami-like wall of water gouged a path through the border region between Nepal and Tibet, sweeping away entire villages.
Here are the latest developments after Wednesday's disaster:
- TRAUMA 'ENORMOUS' -
The level of trauma cascading from the Nepal flash floods is "enormous", the Red Cross said Friday, with early estimates suggesting 93,000 people may have been affected and that the death toll will continue to rise.
"Due to roads and bridges having been washed out and both cell coverage and electricity cuts, we have not yet been able to access some of the hardest-hit areas," said David Fisher, International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies head of delegation for Nepal. "The trauma of this event is enormous."
- RESCUERS REACH TIBET EPICENTRE -
Rescuers in the autonomous Chinese region of Tibet have reached the main area wiped out by the devastating mudslide, Chinese state media reported.
"At approximately 4.30pm (0830 GMT) on Aug 28, six members of the first response team from the Fire and Rescue Corps of Tibet and 15 members and one dog from the first response team of the Fire and Rescue Corps of Sichuan arrived at the border area... They are the first professional teams to reach the core rescue site," Xinhua news agency reported.
- DEATH TOLL HITS 584 -
Nepal's disaster agency said Friday that at least 579 people had been killed, while China reported five, for a total of at least 584.
- MORE THAN 2,400 MISSING -
Nepal's disaster authority raised sharply the number of missing to 1,924 Friday.
The latest figures from Chinese officials on Thursday put the number missing there 558, bringing the total missing on both sides of the border to 2,482.
Those missing include 517 foreigners, as well as 933 workers on hydropower projects on the rivers, according to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
- NEW FLOODS RISK -
Nepal issued a warning to move to higher ground after a dam in Tibet was reported to have burst.
China also halted rescue efforts, with state media saying a lake formed by immense piles of debris had begun overflowing. State media later said the risk from that lake was "decreasing" and rescue operations were proceeding "in an orderly manner."
It was not immediately clear if the lake was the same as the dam that Nepalese authorities warned had burst.
- NEPAL APPEALS FOR AID -
Nepal appealed Friday for international financial assistance, but said it was coping without foreign rescue teams.
"It is not that we will not need help, but our security network is capable and working effectively right now," foreign ministry spokesman Lok Bahadur Chhetri told AFP. "If Nepal needs any specialised help or expertise, then we will request it."
Chinese President Xi Jinping offered Beijing's help Friday.
- EU PLEDGES 2 MILLION EUROS -
The European Union on Friday promised two million euros (US$2.3m) in aid.
European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen wrote on X that the "immediate humanitarian aid" would help "deliver life-saving assistance to families and communities hit hardest."
- STRANDED TOURISTS EVACUATED -
Rescuers have evacuated 555 stranded tourists from Tibet, Chinese state media reported.
CCTV said that 499 residents and 555 tourists had been transported out of the disaster zone as of Friday morning. It did not give the tourists' nationalities.
- 100 TRAPPED IN TUNNEL -
The Nepali military has located people trapped in the tunnel of Trishuli 3A hydropower project, where they were working to bring out survivors.
"Two helicopters have been dispatched but it is challenging because it is tough to even locate the entry points of the tunnel," army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.
Some 350 workers and residents have been brought to safety from the site, he added, but there were more than 100 people trapped in the same area.
- BODIES FOUND DOWNSTREAM -
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Thieves buy tickets before plundering necklace from Vienna museum
Article:
VIENNA:  Two men bought tickets to enter Vienna's Museum of Applied Arts (MAK) before smashing a display case, grabbing a 200-carat platinum and diamond necklace and walking away, police said Friday.
Austrian media said the Van Cleef and Arpels necklace, with 673 precious stones, was worth several million dollars. It is the latest in a series of high-profile heists to hit European museums.
Police said the two men did not wear masks, paid to enter the museum and were clearly seen on surveillance cameras in Thursday's heist.
They "smashed a glass display case" with a hammer before "fleeing with the jewellery in an unknown direction," said a police statement.
The MAK museum confirmed the theft but said it would not comment while the investigation went ahead.
The necklace had been part of an exhibition devoted to the French designers Van Cleef and Arpels. Some 500 pieces had been on display since June.
The exhibition is scheduled to end on Sept 27.
Despite the MAK announcing the exhibition would remain closed until further notice, the wing where the theft occurred reopened hours later.
AFP saw the smashed display case covered with a blue panel but no notice on it explained the theft.
The stolen necklace was designed for the former Egyptian royal family, and was worn by Queen Nazli in 1939 for the marriage of her daughter Faiza to the future Shah of Iran, Mohammad Reza Pahlavi.
On its website, Van Cleef and Arpels called the stolen piece a "triumph of white jewellery."
The French company did not immediately comment on the theft.
European museums have been hit by a series of spectacular thefts since thieves in October broke into the Louvre museum in Paris in broad daylight, escaping in less than eight minutes with jewellery worth $102 million.
Thieves on Thursday raided the Treasure of Villena – one of the greatest Bronze Age gold collections – at a museum in the Spanish city of Villena, taking most of the 50-plus mainly gold bracelets, bowls, bottles and other items on display.
Four works "of extraordinary value" by Renaissance artist Antonello da Messina were stolen from a museum in Sicily, Italy's culture ministry said Sunday.
Two days earlier, Italian police said they had recovered paintings by Renoir, Cezanne and Matisse worth over US$10.4 million which were stolen from the Magnani-Rocca Foundation museum near Parma.

Title: Media Prima newspaper printing operations return to Klang Valley from Sept 1
Article:
KLANG: Media Prima Berhad's newspaper printing operations will return to the Klang Valley from Sept 1, aimed at improving printing and logistics efficiency and speeding up newspaper deliveries to the market.
The New Straits Times Press (M) Berhad (NSTP) chief operating officer Luqman Adrine Ja'afar said the Klang Valley's central location in Peninsular Malaysia would provide an advantage for distribution operations while offering greater flexibility to the printing division.
"The increased operational efficiency is expected to enable newspapers to reach the market faster and give Media Prima's newspaper publications an advantage.
"When we become more efficient, we hope newspapers can reach the market faster. This will give us an advantage over other publications," he said when met during an NSTP management visit to observe the pre-trial newspaper printing operation in Klang here today.
Also present were Media Prima group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali; Media Prima News and Current Affairs Deputy Group Managing Editor Datuk Farrah Naz Abd Karim; Berita Harian (BH) group editor Zulkilfi Jalil; NSTP general manager of newspaper sales and distribution M Prakash; Harian Metro group editor Husain Jahit; and Print Towers Sdn Bhd (PTSB) head of production Adi Sarif Mohamed Anuar.
Luqman said the operation would also be supported by sufficient skilled personnel to ensure a smooth printing process.
On the future of the print media industry, he said newspapers continued to play an important role despite the wide range of digital platforms available to the public.
He said print media remained particularly relevant to communities with limited access to digital communication, especially in rural areas.
"I believe its future is bright because print media provides accurate information, and the news published in newspapers is credible and has been verified by our editors," he said.
Luqman said every news report published underwent a verification process to ensure the information delivered to readers was accurate and reliable.
He said newspaper content also went beyond news, encompassing educational material that could help students develop critical thinking skills.
"To publish a news report in a newspaper, we need a thorough verification process because we cannot print something we are unsure about.
"Our newspaper content is educational. Obtaining credible and accurate news helps students develop stronger critical thinking skills rather than relying solely on information from digital media, where we may not be able to verify its accuracy and authenticity," he said.
Luqman said BH was currently distributed to all secondary schools nationwide, while its newspaper had previously also been distributed to primary schools nationwide, covering about 6,000 schools.
For the New Straits Times (NST), he said programmes such as 'Heard The News' were also provided to help students improve their English proficiency.
"Media Prima's newspapers are not just about news. Besides news, they provide readers with opportunities to learn better, communicate better and develop better thinking skills," he said.
Meanwhile, the Klang Valley printing operation is currently undergoing a trial phase following the completion of equipment and system installations.
The printing operation will begin at about 3pm and may continue until 3am.
The overall printing process could be completed as early as midnight or as late as 7am before the newspapers are distributed to the market.
Previously, the printing operation was carried out in Prai and will end on Aug 31.
The Klang Valley operation will officially begin on Sept 1 following a trial period of more than two weeks to ensure all systems and production processes are running smoothly.

Title: Cambodia says no online scam compounds remain, experts skeptical
Article:
PHNOM PENH: The Cambodian government has claimed a milestone in its fight against the scam industry accused of stealing billions of dollars from victims around the world, with officials saying they have eradicated all scam compounds in the country.
Chhay Sinarith, the senior minister in charge of combatting online scams, told a gathering of foreign diplomats on Thursday that "large-scale scam activities have been brought fully under control, and there are currently no online scam compounds remaining in the country," according to a statement about the minister's meeting released on Friday.
However, criminal groups have moved to decentralised, small-scale activities, hiding in guesthouses, condominiums, rental houses, vehicles, and coffee shops, the statement said.
Cambodian authorities were continuing to target those operations, it said.
Amnesty International's co-regional director Montse Ferrer said the human-rights group was "highly skeptical of suggestions the scamming compound industry has been effectively eliminated" because of the multibillion-dollar industry's entrenched links in the country.
"The true test of long-term success is not how many compounds have closed, but whether the actors responsible have been investigated, prosecuted and prevented from resuming operations," she said.
Compounds, which are mostly run by Chinese criminal gangs and house tens of thousands of workers, many trafficked and living ​under brutal conditions, have proliferated across Cambodia, Laos, the Philippines, and lawless areas along the Myanmar-Thai border since the pandemic.
Reuters has not independently confirmed the government's claim. Reuters journalists who visited abandoned or seized scam centres ‌in ⁠Cambodia in February, March and April and interviewed people involved found evidence of abuse and industrial-scale fraud that has fleeced billions of dollars from victims around the world.
Since July 2025, Cambodian authorities have investigated 793 suspected locations, leading to crackdowns on 624 sites and the detention of nearly 30,000 suspects representing 39 nationalities, Chhay Sinarith said.
"International pressure has produced real disruption this year to the large compounds that long formed the visible front end of Cambodia's state-abetted scam economy," said Jacob Sims, a visiting fellow at Harvard University and an analyst on transnational crime in Southeast Asia.
However, repression of civil society and media in the country meant "claims of eradication with no independent verification must be viewed with skepticism," he said.
"The bigger risk for the international community is confusing visible disruption with dismantling the underlying networks and political protection that made the industry possible."

Title: Umno invites Pas leaders to 2026 general assembly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will invite Pas' top leadership to its 2026 general assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, scheduled for Sept 9 to 12.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision was reached at the party's Supreme Council meeting last night.
"The meeting agreed to extend an official invitation to the top Pas leadership to attend the 2026 Umno General Assembly as a gesture of respect and to reciprocate the invitation extended to the Umno leadership to attend the Pas Muktamar," he told reporters after the meeting.
Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan previously said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi was among the senior leaders invited to the party's 72nd Muktamar from Sept 2 to 5.
Takiyuddin reportedly said three other senior Umno leaders had also been invited.
Zahid confirmed on Aug 23 that Umno would send representatives to the Muktamar, although the party had yet to decide who would attend.
The Pas Muktamar will be held in Kota Baru, Kelantan, with its main event to be opened by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang on Sept 4.
Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has also confirmed that he will attend the Pas Youth Muktamar on Sept 3.
His attendance follows an invitation from Pas Youth to the Umno Youth leadership, providing an opportunity for both wings to meet at an official event.
On the Umno assembly, Asyraf said the Supreme Council had approved three programmes to be held on Sept 8, a day before it begins.
They are the 2026 Malay Education Convention, the Malaysian Islamic Scholars Multaqa and the Creative Women's Pavilion.
"All three programmes scheduled for Sept 8 will be open to the public," he said.

Title: UiTM must remain accessible to underprivileged Bumiputera students - Sultan Sharafuddin
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah wants Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) to remain a gateway to social mobility for Malay and Bumiputera youths from low-income families and rural areas.
His Royal Highness said that as UiTM grew and progressed, the target group for whom the institution was originally established should not be left behind or distanced from higher education opportunities.
"The children of farmers, fishermen, drivers, factory workers, or poor rural families must continue to be assured that if they have the ability and determination to pursue knowledge, UiTM will provide the path to transform their future.
"That is the core spirit of UiTM's struggle that must never be lost," His Royal Highness said at the UiTM 2026 Royal Address at Dewan Konsert Seri Budiman here today.
Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, was also in attendance.
The event, organised by the Chair of the Malay Rulers Institution under the Adiwangsa Empowerment Office, was also attended by Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the establishment of UiTM had paved a path that was previously difficult for many to access, adding that these efforts bore fruit after the institution, which formed the foundation of today's UiTM, started in 1965 with only about 219 students and 11 lecturers.
His Royal Highness noted that within a decade, student enrolment grew to nearly 7,000 while teaching staff increased to about 1,000, with the university offering around 60 academic programmes and expanding branch campuses to several states.
"Today, UiTM has grown into one of the largest higher learning institutions in the country, producing more than 40,000 graduates annually, while its total alumni network has surpassed one million people.
"With such a vast network, I am confident the contributions of alumni can be leveraged to create a more significant impact. Therefore, I propose that a system be developed to enable each alumnus to contribute at least RM10 a month or RM100 a year to UiTM as a token of appreciation for the institution's service during their studies.
"I believe a RM10 monthly contribution is not burdensome and can be afforded by every alumnus. Consider it a sacrifice to ensure the continuity and progress of UiTM," said His Royal Highness.
Sultan Sharafuddin said the fund, with the potential to raise up to RM100 million annually, could be used for UiTM's development and to assist new and existing students facing financial hardship.
"This is where the 'UiTM Dihatiku' slogan, often chanted by students, academic staff, and alumni, can be meaningfully demonstrated. Beyond the statistics are Malay and Bumiputera children from underprivileged backgrounds who have successfully transformed their lives through education at UiTM.
"Today, UiTM graduates are everywhere, in almost every industry and sector. They are accountants, engineers, doctors, lawyers, architects, academics, entrepreneurs, civil servants, corporate figures, artists, media practitioners, and leaders in various fields.
"Some of them lead major organisations, build businesses, create jobs, and contribute directly to national development.
"This is the true measure of UiTM's success, not merely the number of students, graduates, or alumni, but the extent to which the institution has transformed lives and contributed to the nation's progress," His Royal Highness added.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt to continue upholding UiTM's role in Bumiputera development – Zambry
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The government will continue to uphold Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) as a key institution in the educational, professional and socioeconomic development of the Bumiputera community.
Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM's establishment and development would continue to be preserved by the government.
"It is with the awareness of this great responsibility that I wish to affirm that the government will continue to defend UiTM as a key institution in the educational, professional and socioeconomic development of the Bumiputera community.
"The mandate and identity that formed the basis for UiTM's establishment and development will continue to be preserved, but defending UiTM does not mean merely preserving what already exists. Instead, we must continue to strengthen, empower and advance it," he said in his address at Majlis Titah Diraja UiTM 2026 held at Dewan Konsert Seri Budiman here today.
Also in attendance at the ceremony, themed 'Kecemerlangan Institusi Pendidikan Teras Pembangunan Negara', were the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, and the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin.
Zambry said among the strategic measures implemented was the establishment of the UiTM Rationalisation Coordination Committee (URCC) to review academic, research, innovation, governance and talent development aspects.
He said the committee also covers industry linkages, internationalisation, and readiness to face future technological and economic changes, under the leadership of its chairman, Tan Sri Idris Jusoh.
"We want UiTM to continue developing as a 'Premier University Driving Bumiputera Professionals', with a strong mandate, high standards of excellence and broad contributions to the country and the world.
"In conjunction with UiTM's 1956-2026 seven-decade evolution, themed 'Legasi Ilmu, Aspirasi Unggul', the achievements of these seven decades should not merely be celebrated but must be regarded as a responsibility to chart the next seven decades," he said.
At the same time, Zambry stressed that the key question now was not merely how far UiTM had come, but rather the direction that the esteemed institution would take next. – BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: Change of plans saves German family of four
Article:
KATHMANDU: A German family of four narrowly escaped death in Nepal's devastating flash floods, rescued by army helicopter after a last‑minute change of trekking plans spared them from disaster.
Manuel Münch, 37, his Nepali wife, 35, and their two children aged 10 and 7 were airlifted to safety after sheltering with relatives near Trishuli Bazar for days, cut off by destroyed roads and bridges.
The family had been on a short trekking tour in the Langtang region but returned early when landslides blocked paths. A day later, the flood struck.
"We saw the flood wave and then ran up the hill with everything we had," Münch told dpa, describing how they sprinted 800 metres to escape.
From their relatives' house near the river, they heard the disaster approaching. "A loud thunder, a rumbling," Münch said, recalling clouds of dust as the flood wave surged past.
"If we had carried out our trekking tour as planned, we would have spent the night in Syabrubesi that day and would have died," he said.
More than 20 bridges along a 40km stretch were destroyed, cutting off all road access. The family contacted the German embassy for evacuation assistance and was flown to an army camp in Battar Bazar.
Now, they say their only wish is to return to Germany as quickly as possible.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia escalates battle against fires, putrid haze
Article:
PALANGKARAYA: Indonesia has intensified efforts to fight wildfires with cloud seeding and water bombing as thousands of people countrywide battle to breathe in the smoke and haze, officials said on Friday.
More than five million people on Borneo and Sumatra islands were directly exposed to the risks of a putrid haze coming off dozens of fires across the vast archipelago, according to deputy health minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono.
Some 13,500 people were treated for respiratory infections in July and August, Dante said.
Several schools had been closed intermittently and the haze has also made people in Singapore and Malaysia unwell.
"Vulnerable groups that must be evaluated are children, the elderly, pregnant women with asthma and outdoor workers," Dante said.
NGOs have set up two shelters in Palangkaraya, the capital of Central Kalimantan on Borneo island, for babies and children affected by the haze, with more planned.
The shelters, which can accommodate only five children at a time, were equipped with baby formula and oxygen tanks, medicines, and a playground.
Katharina Abi, 30, brought her two small children, aged one and five, to one of the shelters on Friday as thick smoke blanketed their home.
"There's a lot of smoke at my house. In the morning it's not too bad, but in the afternoon and evening there's so much dust, like there's a fire nearby. It really bothers my breathing," she told AFP.
"My children often have coughs and colds, maybe because there is a lot of smoke."
Dante said prolonged exposure to toxic air can cause serious longer-term health complications.
He said the ministry has distributed more than five million masks across Indonesia – a country of 289 million people dealing with the effects of a super-charged El Nino weather event dubbed "Godzilla."
Disaster agency BNPB said on Friday the government has intensified efforts to battle wildfires, with some success.
[[nid:1520975]]
"Cloud seeding remains one of the measures to support efforts to tackle forest and land fires.
"Its implementation depends heavily on atmospheric conditions and the presence of rain-bearing clouds in the target areas," BNPB spokesman Berton Suar Pelita Panjaitan told AFP.
"However, cloud seeding is not the only effort, because the ground and air task forces continue working in the field to carry out extinguishing and cooling operations," he said.
The agency said it has poured more than four million litres of water on burning areas in the recent weeks, and on Wednesday alone it scattered more than 8,000 kilogrammes of salt onto clouds.
Cloud seeding involves sprinkling silver iodide, salts or other particles into clouds to trigger precipitation.
Such operations this week succeeded in prompting light to moderate rains over east and south Sumatra and west Kalimantan, Berton said.
Fires between January and July burned more than 200,000 hectares of land – an area three times the size of the capital Jakarta, the government said last week.
That is more than during previous El Nino seasons in 2019 and 2023.
El Nino is a naturally occurring climate phenomenon that brings worldwide changes in winds, air pressure and rainfall patterns – typically experienced as drought in Indonesia.
Many wildfires in Indonesia are blamed on slash-and-burn land-clearing practices for agriculture.
"We hope the government will immediately address the root causes behind the haze that returns every year," Indra Syahnanda of the WALHI environmental advocacy group told AFP.
"The people of West Kalimantan remain haunted by the haze and have to breathe unhealthy air."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal-Tibet floods: 2,482 missing as death toll hits 584
Article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal: More than 2,400 people were still missing Friday missing and 584 were confirmed dead after flash floods and landslides hit the Nepal-Tibet border.
The figures are likely to continue changing, which is not uncommon in the chaos after a major disaster.
Here are the latest numbers:
- IN TOTAL: 2,482 MISSING -
Nepal's disaster agency on Friday dramatically increased the total number of people missing on its side of the border to 1,924.
Chinese officials have not given updated figures Friday for the total number of missing in Tibet. On Thursday, they put the number at 558.
Together, the total missing Friday was therefore at least 2,482, a leap of more than 1,000 from a day earlier.
Nepal's disaster agency on Friday said that 517 foreigners – which could include tourists as well as foreign workers – were still missing.
Chinese officials on Thursday put the number of foreigners missing at 260.
Together, that means the total number of foreigners missing in the region was at least 777.
Nepal's tourism board on Friday put the number of tourists still "out of communication" at 622.
Of those, 473 were foreign tourists.
The tourism board also said 121 tourists had been rescued. The total number of rescued in the disaster, including residents and foreign workers in the region, was unclear.
Nepal's disaster agency said Friday that at least 579 people had been killed, while China reported five, for a total of at least 584.
- NEPAL -
The new Nepal Tourism Board figures Friday said that 149 Nepali tourists were among the 622 it listed as missing.
The Nepal disaster agency put the figure lower, at 127.
It was not immediately clear how many Nepali residents of the area were unaccounted for, but the figure is believed to be in the hundreds.
- CHINA -
China's foreign ministry said Thursday that nearly 100 Chinese nationals were among the missing in Nepal.
The Nepal Tourism Board said eight Chinese were unaccounted for but that 16 had been rescued.
That was in addition to the 558, including 260 foreigners, missing on the Chinese side of the border.
- INDIA -
Nepal's new tourism board figures Friday showed 98 people from India were missing, but 85 others rescued.
- UNITED STATES -
Ninety US citizens were missing, the State Department said Thursday, adding that three had been rescued and it was not aware of any US fatalities.
The Nepal Tourism Board put the figure at 65 missing on Friday, and two rescued.
- UKRAINE -
The Nepal Tourism Board put the number of Ukrainians still missing Friday at 61.
Ukraine's foreign ministry said on Thursday evening that the total number of Ukrainians missing was 56.
- MALAYSIA -
The Nepal Tourism Board put the number at 51.
- AUSTRALIA -
The number of Australian nationals missing has risen to 39, its foreign ministry said Friday. The Nepal Tourism Board put the figure at 35.
- UNITED KINGDOM -
Thirty-three people from the United Kingdom were missing, the Nepal Tourism Board figures showed Friday.
- LATVIA -
Twenty-nine Latvians were missing, the Nepal Tourism Board said Friday.
- CANADA -
The Nepal Tourism Board said 25 Canadians were among the missing on Friday. Canada's foreign ministry put the figure at 30 in both Nepal and Tibet.
- SOUTH KOREA -
The Nepal Tourism Board said Friday that nine South Korean tourists were missing.
South Korea's foreign ministry said Wednesday they had no news of nine hydropower workers.
- SINGAPORE -
Nine Singaporeans were unaccounted for, the Nepal Tourism Board said.
- GERMANY -
Eight German citizens are missing, according to the Nepal Tourism Board.
- RUSSIA -
Nine Russians are unaccounted for, while two have been rescued, the Nepal Tourism Board said Friday.
- OTHER NATIONALITIES -
South Africa: six (Nepal Tourism Board)
Japan: five (Nepal Tourism Board)
New Zealand: five (foreign ministry and Nepal Tourism Board)
France: four (Nepal Tourism Board)
Spain: three (Spanish foreign ministry)
Belgium: two, and one person rescued (Nepal Tourism Board)
Hungary: three (Hungarian foreign ministry). The Nepal Tourism Board put the figure at one.
Portugal: three, with two found safe (Portuguese government). The Nepal Tourism Board said only one Portuguese citizen was missing
Netherlands: two (Nepal Tourism Board)
Italy: three missing (Italian foreign ministry). The Nepal Tourism Board said Friday one was missing, with two rescued
Ireland: two (Nepal Tourism Board)
Kazakhstan: three (Nepal Tourism Board)
Belarus: one (Nepal Tourism Board)
Finland: one (Nepal Tourism Board)
Israel: one (Nepal Tourism Board)
Lithuania: one (Nepal Tourism Board)
Philippines: one (Nepal Tourism Board)
Serbia: one (Nepal Tourism Board)
Switzerland: one, with one person rescued (Nepal Tourism Board)
Sweden: one (Swedish foreign ministry and Nepal Tourism Board)
Vietnam: one (Nepal Tourism Board)
- NATIONALITIES UNCONFIRMED -
The missing figure released Thursday by China from its side of the border included 260 foreigners, but no breakdown on nationalities was provided.
The nationalities of the non-tourists in Nepal have also not been provided.--AFP

Title: [UPDATED] Those detained for investigations must not be presumed guilty: Asyraf
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  Individuals detained for investigations must not be treated as guilty before they are tried and convicted in court, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said.
"Any attempt to humiliate or insult someone, including by creating the perception that an individual detained for investigation is already guilty, is contrary to the principles of justice, the presumption of innocence and the rule of law," he told reporters after the Umno Supreme Council meeting here today.
Asyraf said Umno would not shield anyone involved in wrongdoing, abuse or misconduct, including its members and leaders, who must face justice through due legal process.
"The rule of law must always be respected and upheld. A person cannot be considered guilty until they have been tried and convicted under the laws in force.
"Umno has consistently maintained that it will not compromise by defending any wrongdoing, abuse or misconduct committed by anyone, including its members and leaders.
"Those involved must be brought to justice through the legal process," he added.
The meeting also saw Negri Sembilan Umno information chief Datuk Ismail Lasim appointed and sworn in as an Umno Supreme Council member.
On a separate matter, Asyraf said Umno would invite Pas' top leadership to attend the 2026 Umno General Assembly from Sept 9 to 12.
He said the invitation was a gesture of respect and reciprocated Pas' invitation to Umno leaders to attend its annual assembly.
"The invitation is a gesture of respect and reciprocates the invitation extended to the Umno leadership to attend the Pas Muktamar," he said.
Asyraf said the Supreme Council had also approved three programmes to be held on Sept 8, a day before the assembly begins.
They are the 2026 Malay Education Convention, the Malaysian Islamic Scholars Multaqa and the Creative Women's Pavilion.
"All three programmes scheduled for Sept 8 will be open to the public," he said.
The four-day Umno General Assembly will be held at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.

Title: Green light for Umno state leaders to hold election talks, trust key: Asyraf
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno state leaders have been given the green light to hold talks with political parties on possible cooperation in upcoming elections.
However, any agreement must be based on sincerity and trust, said Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
"Any negotiations with political parties on cooperation in the coming elections must be based on sincerity and trust, not threats or intimidation," he told reporters after the Umno Supreme Council meeting here today.
Asyraf said the party's leadership also took note of studies by various agencies and academics on public sentiment towards the country's political landscape.
"The findings point particularly to the aspirations of the Malays for Muslim unity to be realised, and for Malay interests and their position to form the foundation of the country's political stability," he said.
His remarks come amid uncertainty over whether the Umno-led Barisan Nasional will cooperate with Pakatan Harapan (PH) or Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the coming Melaka election.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi previously said the coalition intended to defend all 21 seats it won in the 2021 state election while remaining open to electoral cooperation.
BN won 21 of the 28 seats in the election, while PH secured five and PN two.

Title: Selangor Sultan wants UiTM academic programmes to be relevant with global changes
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah wants Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) academic programmes to always remain relevant to global changes so that graduates are competitive in an increasingly challenging job market.
His Royal Highness said this was particularly important in fields such as digital technology, artificial intelligence, science, engineering, medicine, finance, accounting, law, creative industries as well as new fields that would determine the future of the country's economy.
"In the past, the struggle was to gain a place at university, today the struggle is to ensure that our graduates are able to compete and become the best in an increasingly challenging world.
"I want UiTM to continue to uphold its original mandate of empowering the Malays and Bumiputera. But upholding that mandate does not mean that we should turn a blind eye to our own weaknesses or feel satisfied with what has been achieved," the Sultan said in his royal address at the UiTM Royal Address 2026 themed 'Excellence of Educational Institutions as the Core of National Development' at the Seri Budiman Concert Hall here today, in the presence of Raja Permaisuri Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin and Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
Sultan Sharafuddin expressed pride regarding UiTM's achievements, as it has nurtured graduates into key drivers, corporate figures and prominent leaders at the national and global levels.
"UiTM's ability to produce Bumiputera professionals is no longer rhetoric, but a reality proven by clear figures," His Royal Highness said.
The Sultan also stressed on the need for UiTM to produce more job creators and economic owners, rather than merely job seekers.
His Royal Highness pointed out that while UiTM previously played a major role in producing the Bumiputera professional class, the institution in future needed to help produce more entrepreneurs, innovators, scientists, industry leaders and business owners capable of competing at the regional and international levels.
"UiTM's relationship with industry must also be strengthened. Do not let us produce graduates with a degree but without the skills, confidence, language proficiency, thinking ability and capabilities required by industry," the Sultan said, as he urged every UiTM student and graduate to master at least two foreign languages to increase their competitiveness in the job market.
Sultan Sharafuddin also explained that UiTM had a position closely linked to the framework of the Federal Constitution, pointing out that the Universiti Teknologi MARA Act 1976 (Act 173), particularly Section 1A, provides for the establishment of UiTM in accordance with Article 153 of the Federal Constitution.
"Article 153(8A) also allows for the reservation of places in institutions of higher education for Malays and natives of Sabah and Sarawak.
"Therefore, UiTM's role in empowering Malay and Bumiputera education has a clear constitutional foundation, and is not merely an ordinary administrative policy," His Royal Highness said.
The Sultan said any proposal to change the foundation, identity or objectives of UiTM could not be regarded as an ordinary administrative decision, but instead needed to be examined within the framework of the Federal Constitution as a whole.
"At the same time, defending UiTM does not mean denying the educational rights of other races. Malaysia has various higher education institutions for all citizens.
"UiTM was born out of a historical need to narrow the educational and socioeconomic gap among Malays and Bumiputera. As long as this gap still exists, its founding mandate has yet to be completed," His Royal Highness said.
– BERNAMA

Title: Tour bus driver tests positive for drugs following seven-vehicle crash
Article:
PETALING JAYA: A tour bus driver involved in a seven-vehicle crash at the Jalan Lapangan Terbang Subang exit towards the Federal Highway here today tested positive for methamphetamine.
The driver, in his forties, was also found to have a record with 29 previous offences.
Petaling Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said the driver would be brought before the Petaling Jaya Magistrates' Court tomorrow for a remand application.
An initial urine screening test found that the driver tested positive for methamphetamine, he said.
"The driver will be brought to the Petaling Jaya Court tomorrow for a remand application," he said in a statement today.
Shamsudin said police earlier detected a viral social media video showing the seven-vehicle crash, which occurred at about 9.15am.
Preliminary investigations found that the bus, which was travelling from Shah Alam towards Petaling Jaya, lost control before hitting two vehicles, triggering collisions involving four other vehicles.
A local man in his 30s was injured in the crash and taken to Sungai Buloh Hospital for further treatment.
"The bus was carrying no passengers at the time of the incident," he said.
Shamsudin said the case was being investigated under Section 44(1A) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He reminded road users to comply with traffic laws to prevent accidents, adding that police would take stern action against those who violated the law.
Witnesses or those who were at the scene have been urged to visit the nearest police station or contact traffic investigating officer Inspector Mohd Nazreen Nasharuddin at 03-7966 2222 to assist investigations.
Earlier, media reports said a man was injured after being trapped in a car involved in a collision with a tour bus and other vehicles along Jalan Subang towards the Federal Highway.

Title: Wawasan names 160 divisional pro-tem leaders nationwide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) today announced 160 divisional pro-tem chiefs who will oversee the party's affairs at division and state levels nationwide.
The appointments were formalised during a credential presentation ceremony here this afternoon, officiated by Wawasan secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah and attended by the party's leadership.
Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal was among those appointed, taking charge as the Wawasan Machang divisional pro-tem chief.
Also receiving their appointment credentials were Sungai Manik assemblyman Datuk Zainol Fadzi Paharudin, who will lead the Pasir Salak division, Fathul Huzir Ayob for Gerik, and Saifuddin for Indera Mahkota.
Bemban assemblyman and Melaka Perikatan Nasional chairman Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub will head the Jasin division, while Muhammad Fadhli Ismail will lead Tambun.
In June, Reset Movement founder and Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin announced the formation of Wawasan in Tanah Merah, Kelantan.
The former Bersatu deputy president said the establishment of Wawasan was in line with efforts to fulfil the aspirations of the New National Consensus.
Meanwhile, Wawasan vice-president Wan Saiful Wan Jan described the announcement of the divisional leadership line-up as a major achievement, saying it demonstrated that the party's grassroots organisational structure was growing stronger.
"Each pro-tem division now carries the major responsibility of recruiting at least 1,000 members within the stipulated period and establishing branches based on polling district centres (PDM) in their respective parliamentary constituencies to ensure the election machinery is ready," he said in a statement today.
Wan Saiful said appointments for the division's Women and Youth chiefs would be made later together with the party president.
"Wawasan remains committed to presenting a Malaysian face by embracing the demographic diversity of local communities.
"The pro-tem leadership line-up appointed today not only comprises corporate figures, academics, former senior government officers and NGO activists, but also fresh faces making their mark in the political arena," he said.

Title: Fresh flood threat hampers rescue of 558 missing in Tibet
Article:
BEIJING: Risks of renewed flooding, heavy rain and roads covered in mud are complicating the search for hundreds of people missing in Tibet, two days after a deadly mudslide struck the China-Nepal border.
The first rescuers reached the worst-hit site in Tibet on Friday afternoon, Chinese state media reported.
Their arrival came more than 50 hours after a wave of mud and debris crashed across the border into the trade hub of Gyirong on Wednesday morning.
The death toll in Tibet from the mudslide rose from three to five by Friday afternoon, with 558 people still missing, according to figures released in China.
- SECONDARY DISASTERS -
Chinese officials have warned of "great difficulties" in the rescue operation because the border region remains at risk of secondary disasters.
President Xi Jinping chaired a meeting of top leaders about the rescue, which they said "is facing great difficulties."
"There are still many hidden dangers of glaciers, ice lakes and geological disasters in the surrounding area," state news agency Xinhua quoted the leaders as saying.
A huge lake formed upstream after the mudslide hit on Wednesday, raising concerns that it could burst and cause further severe flooding.
Rescue operations were temporarily paused earlier on Friday due to risks of "secondary disasters" from the lake overflowing, state broadcaster CCTV said.
It said at the time that around "50,000 cubic metres of ice debris have flowed into the... lake", citing footage captured by a military drone.
Hours later, another CCTV report said risks were "gradually decreasing" as water from the lake was "flowing out naturally, with the outflow discharge exceeding the inflow discharge."
The US Geological Survey said the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.
- BURIED ROADS -
Footage from Chinese media on Thursday and Friday showed roads submerged by mud up to three kilometres  from the border, as rescuers climbed over fallen branches and rocks towards the main disaster site.
Rescuers needed to plough through mud at least 1.5 metres thick, according to local media reports on Wednesday.
Officials in Gyirong County asked volunteer groups to refrain from visiting the area to ensure "safe and orderly" rescue operations, according to a statement shared by local media on Friday.
The Tibet Autonomous Region is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, who are generally only allowed to visit on government-organised trips.
Communications at the worst-hit site remained down on Friday.
- DAYS OF RAIN -
Heavy rain and scattered thunderstorms through Monday could further complicate the search.
Local weather authorities on Friday said "heavy rain" would fall in Gyirong Town – where the mudslide struck – through Saturday.
Rain could lighten on Sunday and Monday but the region could also see thunderstorms, the county's weather bureau said.
"The risks of disasters is relatively high," the bureau warned, because continuous rain could cause flash floods and mudslides.
CCTV said that 499 Chinese nationals and 555 foreigners had been transported out of the disaster zone by Friday.--AFP

Title: Iran war enters its endgame with no clear winner
Article:
SIX   months after United States and Israeli forces attacked Iran, killing its supreme leader and maiming his son and successor, the Iranian government is under economic siege, but it still holds power and believes it has time on its side.
A threat by US President Donald Trump to impose crippling new sanctions on Iran faces a fundamental problem: Teheran is betting he will not take the final step to break the stalemate — aggressively enforcing secondary sanctions on the countries keeping its economy afloat, foremost among them China and India.
Washington's latest measures, announced on Monday, mark a new phase in the conflict that began on Feb 28, shifting the battlefield from missiles and air strikes to Iran's oil revenues, banks and trading partners.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has said Washington will cut off the financial lifelines sustaining Iran's economy, while a US-led naval blockade restricts Teheran's oil exports and access to hard currency.
"The (Trump) administration is groping in a sort of desperate fashion to try to find a pathway out of this," said Aaron David Miller, a former US diplomat and senior fellow at Carnegie Endowment.
Bessent invoked the 1944 D-Day landings in France during World War 2 when he unveiled the sanctions, but Miller said: "To me, this isn't D-Day. It's Desperation Day. I don't think the administration is any closer to finding a way out of this."
Michael Knights, head of research at Horizon Engage, a New York-based strategic advisory, said Teheran has spent decades adapting to sanctions and endured previous "maximum pressure" campaigns without altering its behaviour.
He said Iran could increasingly adopt the model used by its Houthi allies in the Red Sea: periodic attacks, intermittent negotiations and a prolonged campaign of disruption short of all-out war, potentially targeting shipping, ports, energy infrastructure or other critical assets to make the conflict increasingly costly for Gulf states to tolerate.
Alan Eyre, a former US diplomat who worked on Iran, questioned whether Washington has the international support and bureaucratic machinery to make the sanctions stick.
He said unlike the multilateral campaign preceding the 2015 nuclear deal between Teheran and major powers, the latest measures rely on public threats rather than sustained diplomacy with allies and trading partners.
Iranian officials dismiss the US strategy as a replay of a playbook that has already failed.
A senior Iranian official said countries such as China would not stop cooperating with Iran simply to serve US interests.
Some political analysts said the strategy faces a deeper flaw: from North Korea to Russia and Iran itself, sanctions have rarely forced governments to abandon goals they view as existential for their survival.
For Iran's rulers, the biggest threat may be the risk that worsening hardship again spills into mass unrest, according to insiders and an Iranian official.
In January, demonstrations over economic hardship were crushed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and the Basij militia, with thousands killed.
The appointment this month of Hossein Taeb, a key architect of previous crackdowns, to lead the Basij was one of the clearest signs yet of official concern about renewed unrest.
The Basij, a paramilitary force affiliated with the IRGC, has repeatedly been deployed by Iran's rulers to suppress protests.
For the Gulf states, the calculation is especially fraught.
They prefer economic and diplomatic pressure to another round of war, but fear an outcome that enables Iran to declare victory while retaining the ability to disrupt traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global oil supply route that Teheran has effectively blocked, pushing up global oil prices.
Abdulaziz Sager, chairman of the Saudi-based Gulf Research Center, said Gulf governments are unconvinced that sanctions alone can rapidly alter Iran's behaviour, given the leadership's resilience and ability to maintain internal control.
Significant political change, or the collapse of Iran's theocratic leadership, he said, is unlikely to come quickly.
The result is a dangerous impasse if mediated talks fail to produce a breakthrough.
Washington wants Iran to abandon its leverage over Hormuz without conceding Teheran a role in managing the waterway, Iran wants the US naval blockade lifted without appearing to surrender, and Gulf states want the conflict contained without letting Iran emerge as the victor.
The Iran war has reached its endgame: a costly stalemate.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Muslims must lead by example through morality, integrity: Anwar
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: Muslims must set the best example for society through good character, integrity, diligence and by rejecting corruption and wrongdoing, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the respect accorded to Muslims should stem from the positive values they demonstrate in daily life, including working diligently, keeping promises and not abusing positions of trust.
"If people see us working hard, displaying good character, not cheating and not stealing money, they will respect us. We must set a good example," he said at a Maulid Akbar ceremony in conjunction with National Day at Masjid Tengah here today.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was also present.
Anwar said Islam carries a message of compassion and goodness for all, and Muslims must therefore safeguard relationships and the welfare of the entire community, regardless of race or religion.
The Prime Minister said Muslims must also demonstrate balance in life by prioritising knowledge, faith, morality, spiritual and physical development, as well as material progress.
He said the development of Malaysia Madani could not depend solely on policies, economic growth or technological advancement without a strong foundation of faith, morality and character.
"While reaching for the sky, we must remain rooted in the earth. Being rooted in the earth means having faith, morality and character, so that our values and moral principles are preserved," he said.
Anwar also stressed the importance of seeking knowledge from Islamic scholars and strengthening ties between religious scholars and leaders through constructive advice and views.
Malaysia Madani must continue to drive economic growth and master modern technology, while ensuring that values and morality remain the pillars of national development, he added.– BERNAMA

Title: Nepal floods trauma 'enormous': Red Cross
Article:
GENEVA: The Nepal-Tibet flood disaster has left an "enormous" level of trauma, the Red Cross said Friday, with early estimates suggesting 93,000 people may have been affected.
The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), the world's largest humanitarian network, fears the death toll from Wednesday's disaster, already above 500, will continue to rise.
"Due to roads and bridges having been washed out and both cell coverage and electricity cuts, we have not yet been able to access some of the hardest-hit areas," said David Fisher, the IFRC head of delegation for Nepal.
"The trauma of this event is enormous," he told a Geneva press conference, speaking from Kathmandu.
"Thousands of homes have been destroyed or suffered significant damage. We believe that at least 93,000 people have been affected and in great need."
Nepal's Red Cross has begun providing emergency relief, including food, water, hygiene kits, mattresses and blankets.
The floods and landslides that struck Nepal and China's autonomous Tibet region saw a tsunami-like wall of water bury homes, smash bridges and sweep away vehicles.
UN aid chief Tom Fletcher said on X that the United Nations was "moving at speed to save lives."
Lila Pieters Yahia, the UN resident coordinator for Nepal, said drinking water was being airlifted into affected areas.
"The damage is just incredible," she told the press conference, speaking from the field, adding that more than 40 bridges had been destroyed or badly damaged and "over 40km of road completely destroyed."
She said search and rescue operations were the government priority.
- 'CASCADING HAZARDS' -
"We haven't seen a mountain hazard event like this for a very, very long time," Kamal Kishore, head of the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, told the press conference.
"It's really immense and we are still coming to grips with the extent the damage."
He said the disaster was still unfolding in an ecosystem where one disaster could trigger "a range of cascading hazards."
The UN children's agency UNICEF, said at least 14 children were confirmed dead.
"Sadly, we're only seeing the beginning of this tragedy," spokesman Ricardo Pires told reporters.
"For those who survived, the emergency is far from over. Children now face increased risks of disease, malnutrition, violence and exploitation, as well as the psychological impact of what they have experienced."
He said 18 schools had been destroyed and another 20 damaged, with an estimated 10,000 children urgently needing support to continue their education.
The World Health Organization said eight health workers were missing and six health facilities had been damaged.
"The priority is to ensure continuity of health services," WHO spokesman Tarik Jasarevic said.
He said the UN health agency had delivered surgical masks and gloves and body bags to Nepal.--AFP

Title: Merdeka is stronger when we stand together
Article:
AUGUST is a particularly auspicious month in our neighbourhood. We in Malaysia celebrate National Day on the last day of the month.
Our near neighbours — Singapore and Indonesia — also commemorate their respective independence days in August.
August is also when the Philippines remembers the martyrdom of Benigno Aquino Sr in 1983, which led to the country's rebirth as a democracy 40 years ago.
While each nation's independence day is a milestone worth celebrating every year, we increasingly live in a rather lawless world where might seems right.
Thus, for smaller nations like ours, it is also worth pondering how interdependence — especially among near neighbours — may actually hold the key towards preserving our independence, moving forward.
There is, for starters, security in numbers. If we can align our policies more closely with near neighbours, such as Indonesia and Singapore, for example, our collective voice in the global arena would carry greater weight, compared with if we individually take a stand.
To be sure, we are all members of Asean, which incidentally also marks its founding every year in August. Asean is sometimes referred to as the most successful of regional groupings.
But Asean, to my mind, is perhaps the most successful non-entity. Its "success" owes much to an endless search for the lowest common denominator among its now 11 members.
Sure, it is a forum for countless meetings each year among its top leaders and government functionaries. The regional grouping has perhaps become too big and unwieldy, unable, therefore, to generate much of an impact on the everyday lives of ordinary people.
That is probably the secret of its success; that it is so innocuous to ordinary citizens of Asean countries.
We are facing transboundary haze originating in Indonesia, impacting many in Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore.
If there is a trilateral forum involving our three nations, apart from the usual Asean forum, will it be more effective in tackling the haze and seeing to it that it does not recur almost yearly?
Amid the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, we should remember another strategic chokepoint, the Strait of Malacca, which touches our three nations.
It is in the collective interest of our three nations to ensure that freedom of navigation through this waterway will never be impeded.
Each of these three neighbouring countries punches above its weight individually in one arena or another. Imagine how much greater that clout can be if we combine our individual strengths and punch an even greater collective weight globally.
We know Asean is where it is because each of its member states is loath to give up any of its own sovereignty for the greater good of the whole.
Perhaps Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia can more easily subsume some of their own national interests for the greater good of all three?
In time, we may even show the way forward for Asean as a whole.
Our respective independence will surely count for more if we can hack more meaningful interdependence.
The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: The sand racket digging Malaysia deeper
Article:
THERE is a crime that is practically hiding in plain sight: illegal sand mining and its nationwide logistics.
Unlike contrabands like drugs, wildlife and fake luxury products, illegal sand mining barely gets any press. This is because the players aren't typical rogues.
They are corporations, builders and concrete mixing plants, feeding greedily into the property boom for decades. But the biggest rogues are nations, consumers and buyers of Malaysia's illegally mined sand, used to build cities through mega land reclamation projects.
Ever since Malaysia banned sea sand exports, sand smuggling syndicates have forged paperwork to dredge sand in certain states, while deep-sea dredging vessels quietly extract and transport sea sand to nearby customers.
Illegal sand mining came to the fore after police arrested 99 people and seized RM119 million worth of minerals, heavy machinery, vehicles and mining equipment during a five-day nationwide crackdown on illegal mining. Under Op Gali Mega, 45 mining sites were inspected in 10 states, revealing 24 illegal operations.
Illegal sand mining has devastating consequences: it causes floods and landslides, long-term damage to rivers, forests and water catchment areas. But it is lucrative, because legal sand is expensive.
Suppliers pay state extraction royalties, pay for Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA), pay corporate taxes and secure official approved permits, with costs passed to buyers.
Illegal sand is cheaper. Syndicates drag heavy machinery to state land or rivers overnight, pay nothing in royalties, while bearing only fuel, labour and bribes, selling lorry-loads at huge discounts.
A legal sand dredging business goes like this: let's say base sand cost is RM42,000, but miners must pay RM3,000 for EIA, levies and permits and RM18,000 in government tax. Total cost: RM67,500. Illegal operators pay RM40,500 in base sand cost without levy, permit and tax payments, saving RM27,000.
Nevertheless, illegal sand mining is  risky. If caught, miners face closure fines of RM50,000, court fines of a minimum RM100,000, seizure of excavators and lorries, and bear rebuilding costs of RM120,000, making it a total loss of RM620,000.
Ever read about collapsed buildings? That's because the illegal sand used is either unwashed or untested and contains high levels of salt, mud or organic trash.
In concrete used to construct buildings, roads or bridges, it prematurely cracks and fails. Illegal sand mining has operated for years with impunity.
The seizures and arrests suggest a wider, organised problem spanning multiple states.
Since standard patrols are useless, detecting illegal sand mining needs modern tracking technology, strict legal enforcement and market-driven alternatives.

Title: MetMalaysia forecasts thunderstorms, rain and haze on national day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a special weather forecast in conjunction with the 2026 National Day celebration, with several states set to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and haze on Aug 31.
According to a graphic posted on MetMalaysia's Facebook page tonight, Selangor, Negri Sembilan, Melaka and Johor are expected to experience thunderstorms in the morning, while Perak, Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan are forecast to have thunderstorms in the afternoon.

Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan are expected to experience haze throughout the day.

The west coast of Sabah, meanwhile, is expected to experience haze throughout the day.
In Sarawak, most areas, including Kuching, Serian, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu, Mukah, Kapit, Bintulu and Miri, are expected to experience haze throughout the day.
Rain is expected to hit Kapit and Miri at night, while thunderstorms are forecast to hit Limbang in the afternoon, followed by rain at night.
In a separate post, MetMalaysia said most areas in the Klang Valley and along the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia are expected to be hazy on Sunday, the eve of the 2026 National Day celebration.
According to the special weather forecast graphic updated tonight, hazy conditions are expected in Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Labuan and Sarawak, as well as Kudat and the west coast of Sabah.
MetMalaysia also forecasts rain in Perak, Pahang, Terengganu, Kelantan and several areas in Sabah, including the interior, Sandakan and Tawau, on that night, while clear conditions are expected in Perlis, Kedah and Penang.
MetMalaysia advised those attending the National Day celebration on Sunday or the National Day parade on Aug 31 to check the weather forecast for their respective locations and take precautions in the event of changes in weather conditions.

Title: Teacher faces 10 charges of sexually assaulting female pupils
Article:
KUCHING: A male teacher has been charged with 10 counts of sexually assaulting 10 female pupils at a primary school in Mukah between 2022 and 2024.
The 56-year-old accused appeared before Judge Musyiri Peet at the Mukah Sessions Court today. No plea was recorded.
He was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16(1) of the same Act.
Section 14(a) carries up to 20 years imprisonment and whipping upon conviction.
Section 16(1), which applies to persons in a relationship of trust with the victims, provides for an additional prison term of up to five years and at least two strokes of the cane.
The court granted the accused bail of RM2,000 for each charge, totalling RM20,000, with two sureties. The accused posted bail.
The court Oct 20 for mention.
Meanwhile, Mukah police chief Deputy Superintendent Muhamad Rizal Alias said the accused was teaching at the primary school when the alleged offences occurred.
He said all the victims were pupils at the school and that the alleged offences took place in a science laboratory and classrooms.
Police received a report on Aug 7 from a counsellor at a secondary school in Mukah after the counsellor received a complaint from one of the victims.
Following the report, a team investigated the matter before arresting the accused to assist in investigations and further action, he said in a statement.

Title: National Day 2026 Prime Minister's address ceremony set for 2pm at PICC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The 2026 National Day Prime Minister's Address Ceremony at the Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) here has been scheduled for 2pm, according to the Ministry of National Unit.
In a statement today, the ministry said the adjustment was made after taking into account current developments, particularly to ensure the safety, health and comfort of guests and the public, in addition to ensuring the smooth implementation of the ceremony.
"The 2026 National Day Prime Minister's 2026 Address Ceremony is an important platform to reflect on the aspirations and hopes of the Madani government leadership in fuelling the spirit of independence, strengthening patriotism, and nurturing a sense of love and responsibility towards the country.
"All Malaysians are invited to attend to celebrate the spirit of National Day and foster the values of mutual understanding, respect and acceptance of diversity towards building a nation that continues to progress, remain harmonious and prosper," the statement said.

Title: Teo denies allegations of involvement in gang-related activities
Article:
KULAI: Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching today denied allegations circulating on social media linking her to gang-related activities in the state and a road accident currently under police investigation.
The DAP national vice-chairman said the allegations were false and baseless, stressing that new social media accounts had been created specifically to make accusations against her.
"I have been in politics for 18 years and have served as a MP for 13 years. There may have been occasions when I met someone once or twice, or perhaps had photographs taken with someone in an ordinary social setting.
"However, to claim that I was involved in such activities is a false accusation because they merely showed photographs of me with someone, when it was simply a normal social activity.
"The police, including the Johor police chief, have already held a press conference and announced that 13 suspects had been arrested. I welcome a thorough investigation by the police," she told reporters after the Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival at Hutan Bandar Putra here today.
– MORE
TEO-DENIAL (SECRET SOCIETY) 2 (LAST) KULAI
Teo, who is also Johor DAP chairman, said the defamatory claims demonstrated that anyone could become a victim of the spread of fake news in the digital era.
She therefore advised the public not to readily believe information received through social media without verifying it first.
"We need to think rationally and investigate first. I myself have lodged a complaint with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) as well as a police report.
"However, the main challenge is that the decision to shut down the account or delete the post rests with Meta, and not all fake news can be removed immediately," she said.

Title: [UPDATED] 36 M'sians in Tibet reported safe, status still being verified: Wisma Putra
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Thirty-six Malaysians in Tibet, China have reported to be safe following flash floods and landslides in the China-Nepal border area.
Foreign Ministry deputy secretary-general (Bilateral Relations) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said that the identities and status of the 36 Malaysians were still being verified with Chinese authorities, and they are cross-checking for any overlap with the list of Malaysians who remained uncontactable in Nepal.
"We are also conducting cross-checks because we have only just received this information... We will provide an update if there are any names that overlap, including the actual number of our citizens who are still missing or have been found safe, whether in Nepal or Tibet," he told Bernama here today.
Following the information, the ministry's coordination efforts had now been expanded to cover areas on the Chinese side of the border, he added.
He shared that the Malaysian Embassy in Beijing and the Malaysian High Commission in New Delhi were also involved in the process as there was information that some Malaysians might have travelled along routes involving China and India.
The Foreign Ministry's Operations Room in Putrajaya would continue to operate round the clock to coordinate information, assist Malaysians in the affected areas and provide the latest updates to family members, Syed Mohamad Hasrin said, adding that they would continue seeking confirmation from Chinese authorities regarding the whereabouts and safety of Malaysians in Tibet before drawing any further conclusions.
On the possibility of bringing affected Malaysians home, he said the matter needed to be coordinated with the Nepali authorities and tour operators, including verifying the status of their travel documents before any further action could be taken.
The priority at present was to locate Malaysians and ensure their safety in the affected areas, while taking into account weather conditions and limited access, he said.
In a related development, he said Malaysia, through the National Security Council (NSC) and the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA), was coordinating and assessing the form of assistance that could be provided to Nepal.
Any assistance would take into account the needs identified by the Nepal government and would be subject to the consideration of NSC, as well as the acceptance and priorities of the Nepal government through official channels.
He said while Malaysia has expressed its readiness to assist Nepal, the Nepal government had so far indicated that it had sufficient resources to conduct search and rescue operations and required assistance could include financial resources and other forms of aid.
Nonetheless, Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the ministry is also assessing the readiness of Malaysian agencies, including the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team, while the Defence Ministry and the Malaysian Armed Forces were also ready to provide assistance.
Finally, in accordance with a decree by Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, the ministry would continue to provide affected Malaysians' family members with the latest verified information.Syed Mohamad Hasrin said.
"At the same time, the media and public are urged not to speculate or disseminate unverified information, but instead refer to official statements from the Foreign Ministry for the latest updates," he said.
Yesterday, Sultan Ibrahim urged Wisma Putra to take all necessary measures regarding Malaysians affected by the major floods in Rasuwa, Nepal. - BERNAMA

Title: Oriental Kopi's Q3 net profit dips 5pct to RM17mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd's net profit fell five per cent to RM17 million in the third quarter (Q3) ended June 30, 2026 from RM17.95 million a year earlier.
This is due to higher raw material and store operating costs compressing margins, while expansion-related expenses pushed up its effective tax rate.
According to its filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company's revenue rose 34.2 per cent to RM156.63 million from RM116.75 million last year.
This was due to the expansion of its café chain alongside its distribution and retail business for packaged food products.
No dividend was declared with the latest quarterly result.
For the nine months period (9M2026), Oriental Kopi's net profit increased 9.4 per cent to RM49.08 million from RM44.86 million last year, while revenue surged 39 per cent to RM443.08 million from RM317.75 million previously.
Oriental Kopi remains optimistic about its prospects, supported by its competitive strengths, strategic business initiatives and favourable market conditions in the food and beverages (F&B) services sector as well as in the distribution and retailing of our brand of packaged foods.
"With these factors in place, the company remains confident in its business growth in the coming financial year and anticipates continued improvements in both revenue and profitability," it added.
