Title: Bird-cage rooms and rooftop dorms expose Malaysia’s migrant housing enforcement gaps
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — From the outside, the 800-square-foot apartment unit looks no different from any other. Yet, what would normally be considered adequate accommodation for a family of five is home to 15 migrant workers.
Some employers are known to rent vacant flats, apartments or houses for their foreign workers, cramming as many of them as possible into each unit simply to cut costs, while failing to provide even basic amenities, including mattresses and kitchen equipment.
There are also landlords and property owners who modify the interiors of their units by either constructing dozens of tiny rooms or installing partitions to create cubicles for their tenants, most of whom are foreign workers.
Some have also resorted to constructing makeshift rooms, where space permits, on the rooftops of shop lots to accommodate foreign workers, particularly those employed in restaurants and supermarkets, and as general workers.
Workers from Myanmar, Vietnam and Cambodia interviewed by Bernama said they did not mind living under such conditions.
“I have to wake up as early as 3am to prepare the raw ingredients in the kitchen before the restaurant opens at 6am,” said Chin (not his real name), a Cambodian national working as a restaurant assistant in Puchong, Selangor.
“At night, after business operations end at 8pm, I have to clean the restaurant… my work only finishes at around 10pm. So, living upstairs makes things easier for me.”
The “hostel” he stays in is located on one of the upper floors of the building that houses the restaurant where he works. It has two rooms, with four male workers sharing one and four female employees the other, along with a bathroom and toilet.
“Originally, there was only one room, but the shop owner installed a partition to turn it into two rooms... we sleep on mattresses on the floor,” he said.
Rooms resembling bird cage pose safety risks
The trend of modifying apartments, shop lots and houses by installing partitions to create tiny cubicles — often metaphorically described as a bird’s cage, bird’s nest or grave — is worrying due to the serious safety risks involved.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government has previously issued stern warnings to house and premises owners engaging in such practices.
Despite the enforcement of amendments to the Employees’ Minimum Standards of Housing, Accommodations and Amenities Act 1990 (Act 446) since 2020, which requires employers to provide their workers with comfortable accommodation and basic amenities, Bernama was informed by various stakeholders that the practice of cramming as many migrant workers as possible into cramped, modified residential units remains widespread.
Commenting on this, senior lecturer in real estate at the Faculty of Built Environment, Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Shah Alam, Muhammad Azwan Sulaiman, said arbitrary modifications to premises could compromise occupants’ safety.
“From a technical and building safety perspective, having overly crowded rooms within a residential unit or premises can pose a serious fire risk.
“The problem is compounded by inadequate ventilation and lighting, turning such homes into potential death traps because, in the event of a fire, thick smoke can be more dangerous than the flames themselves, especially when occupants struggle to identify escape routes in an already congested space,” he told Bernama.
Muhammad Azwan said from an engineering perspective, the additional load arising from excessive numbers of occupants, furniture and electrical equipment could have long-term implications for the structural integrity and utility systems of buildings.
“Furthermore, electricity and water usage exceeding the building’s original design capacity not only increases the risk of electrical wiring-related hazards but can also shorten the building’s lifespan and increase maintenance costs,” he said, adding that the main problem with the practice of subdividing rooms is not the use of partitions but when the return on investment begins to take precedence over habitability and human lives.
Need for clear guidelines
Muhammad Azwan also proposed that the authorities establish clearer guidelines on the types of internal modifications permitted in stratified properties, particularly when such alterations involve the building’s basic structure or common property.
“The aim is not to prevent homeowners from carrying out renovations, but rather to reduce the risk of outset modifications.
“Good design at the planning stage can reduce unauthorised alterations, safety risks and disputes between occupants and management bodies,” he said.
He added that although Malaysia has various legal and regulatory frameworks governing worker accommodation, buildings and strata properties, one of the challenges is that supervisory and enforcement responsibilities fall under the jurisdiction of various agencies.
“This can create gaps in monitoring, particularly when a residential unit gradually becomes a high-density workers’ accommodation facility without obtaining the necessary approvals.
“Therefore, stronger inter-agency coordination, more effective monitoring and consistent enforcement are more important than simply introducing another new law,” he said.
Local authorities must act
While the government’s People’s Housing Projects (PPR) and public housing schemes intended for low-income Malaysians were previously targeted by employers seeking to house their workers, their attention has now shifted to medium-cost apartments and the upper floors of shop lots.
On Aug 3, local media reported that since 2023, 502 premises nationwide had been identified as having been extensively modified to create rental rooms, dubbed “bird’s nests”, that posed a high safety risk, particularly in the event of fire.
Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad was reported as saying that this practice was prevalent in major urban areas in Selangor, Penang and Johor, as well as Kuala Lumpur, due to the high demand for affordable accommodation among workers, students and middle-income groups.
Several integrated operations known as “Op Sarang Burung” conducted in the capital in June and Johor in July also found employers converting part of shop lot rooftops into hostels for foreign workers without approval from the authorities.
The operations in Kuala Lumpur were carried out by the Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department in collaboration with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the police.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh told Bernama in an interview that enforcement operations against residential units and premises illegally converted into rental rooms or hostels for foreign workers should be conducted regularly to ensure compliance with the law.
She said all local authorities should take the responsibility seriously, while close monitoring of enforcement personnel is also necessary to prevent abuse of power in the course of their duties.
“(In Kuala Lumpur) We need coordination among DBKL and the relevant enforcement agencies to ensure employers provide legal and suitable accommodation for their workers, while residential units under public housing schemes such as PPR remain available to families who are genuinely eligible and in need,” she said.
Comply with uniform building by-laws
Meanwhile, Ampang Jaya Municipal Council (MPAJ) deputy president Hasrolnizam Shaari told Bernama that safety aspects are always given priority before the council approves applications and renovation plans submitted by owners of business premises and residential properties.
He said any renovation that alters the layout, use of space or actual occupancy capacity would be assessed based on the Uniform Building By-Laws and the requirements of all local authorities, including MPAJ.
“We have demolished additional structures deemed to be highly risky as they could endanger occupants and the surrounding community because they might obstruct emergency access for fire engines and ambulances, besides causing disputes among residents.
“For structures that do not pose an immediate risk, we will continue to monitor them and take further action if they pose a threat to safety,” he added.
He said stubborn residential property owners who continue to carry out renovation and construction works without the approval of the local authority can be fined up to RM25,000 under Section 70(11) of the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974 (Act 133), while the court can order the local authority to alter or demolish the building.
Section 70(13)(d) of Act 133 further stipulates that any party who fails to comply with a lawful written order or directive issued by the local authority, or any limit or condition imposed by the local authority on renovation works, may be fined up to RM50,000, imprisoned for up to three years, or both.
He said MPAJ also adopts an integrated enforcement approach with other agencies, including the Immigration Department, police, State Health Department and the National Anti-Drugs Agency.
“Sometimes, a house has only one front door, but there are many occupants, both male and female, inside, with the space inside partitioned. So, we use an integrated enforcement approach to monitor and manage such situations,” he said.
Hasrolnizam said a slightly different approach is taken for renovations involving commercial premises, such as shop lots, as these properties are used for business activities.
“If the owner of a commercial lot wants to build seven or eight rooms, the application can be considered from a physical standpoint, but every room must have adequate lighting, ventilation and safety features, particularly in the event of a fire.
“They must first demonstrate that the design is acceptable and can be approved, and then obtain the necessary licence.
“However, if a business premises is found to be operating as a hostel without approval, it constitutes an offence and action can be taken,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Wisma Putra: Two Malaysians found safe after Nepal floods, 55 remain unreachable
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — Two of the 57 Malaysians previously reported as untraceable following flash floods and landslides in Nepal have been located, while 55 others remain unreachable as of 2.22pm today.
Foreign Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Bilateral Affairs) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin said the two Malaysians had been successfully located, but their information and details were still undergoing cross-checking and further verification.
“Out of the 57, two have been reported safe so far,” he told Bernama here today.
He said the cross-checking process was important to confirm the identity, location and actual status of both individuals, and to avoid duplication of information in the list of Malaysians who remained unreachable.
Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the figure of 55 was still subject to further verification based on information received from Nepalese authorities and relevant agencies.
He said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had instructed the ministry to continue monitoring the operations closely and step up efforts to locate the remaining Malaysians.
Following the directive, he said an official from the Malaysian High Commission in Dhaka had been dispatched to Kathmandu to help bolster the operations of the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal.
“The official is assisting in coordinating information, monitoring developments and liaising with the relevant Nepalese authorities,” he said.
According to Syed Mohamad Hasrin, the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu was also collaborating with Nepalese authorities, the Nepalese Foreign Ministry’s emergency response team, the Nepal Tourism Board, relevant agencies and tour operators to obtain and verify information regarding the untraceable Malaysians.
Nepalese authorities reported that 528 individuals had been rescued so far, comprising 490 Nepalese and 38 foreigners. Based on the latest information received, no Malaysians have been identified among those rescued.
The flash floods and landslides in the Rasua district occurred following the overflow of the Bote Koshi River on August 26, causing severe damage to infrastructure, including roads and bridges, as well as disrupting electricity supply and communication networks.
“This situation has made access to the affected areas difficult, thus hampering search and rescue efforts and the gathering of information on Malaysians in those areas,” he said.
Syed Mohamad Hasrin said the ministry was also monitoring safety warnings issued by Nepalese authorities regarding the risk of water overflows from the border areas.
He said the situation in the affected areas remained challenging and safety conditions could change rapidly, while search and rescue operations also faced constraints due to weather conditions and infrastructure damage.
“We are hoping for the best. But under these conditions, it is quite difficult. Their authorities are also dealing with their own affected citizens. The situation is severe, with cut-off roads, damaged bridges and so on,” he said.
The Foreign Ministry’s operations room in Putrajaya is now operating 24 hours a day to coordinate information, assist Malaysians in the affected areas and provide updates to family members.
According to Syed Mohamad Hasrin, every call and piece of information received must be cross-checked with the lists from Nepalese authorities and the ministry’s internal records to avoid duplication or confusion.
The number of unreachable Malaysians was obtained from various sources, including Nepalese authorities, Tourism Malaysia, tour operators and family members.
Within the first two to three hours after the operations room was activated, the ministry received between 12 and 15 calls from family members and friends seeking information on Malaysians believed to be in Nepal.
The ministry urged family members with relevant information to contact the operations room, providing details such as full names, passport numbers, travel itineraries, last known locations and contactable phone numbers.
Malaysians with relevant information can contact the Putrajaya Operations Room at +603 8887 4570 or email dutyofficer@kln.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: ‘False and baseless’: Teo Nie Ching rejects social media claims linking her to Johor gang activity, lodges police report
Article:
KULAI, Aug 28 — Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching today denied allegations circulating on social media linking her to gang-related activities in the state and a road accident currently under police investigation.
The DAP national vice-chairman said the allegations were false and baseless, stressing that new social media accounts had been created specifically to make accusations against her.
“I have been in politics for 18 years and have served as a MP for 13 years. There may have been occasions when I met someone once or twice, or perhaps had photographs taken with someone in an ordinary social setting.
“However, to claim that I was involved in such activities is a false accusation because they merely showed photographs of me with someone, when it was simply a normal social activity.
“The police, including the Johor police chief, have already held a press conference and announced that 13 suspects had been arrested. I welcome a thorough investigation by the police,” she told reporters after the Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival at Hutan Bandar Putra here today.
Teo, who is also Johor DAP chairman, said the defamatory claims demonstrated that anyone could become a victim of the spread of fake news in the digital era.
She therefore advised the public not to readily believe information received through social media without verifying it first.
“We need to think rationally and investigate first. I myself have lodged a complaint with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) as well as a police report.
“However, the main challenge is that the decision to shut down the account or delete the post rests with Meta, and not all fake news can be removed immediately,” she said.
Yesterday, Senai assemblyman Wong Bor Yang lodged a police report at the Kulai District Police Headquarters here over defamatory posts and false allegations linking Teo and DAP to a gang. — Bernama

Title: Stulang assemblyman Andrew Chen returns to lead Johor Opposition after bruising state election
Article:
KULAI, Aug 28 — Johor Pakatan Harapan (PH) has agreed to appoint Stulang state assemblyman Andrew Chen Kah Eng as Johor’s Leader of the Balancing Force (Ketua Pengimbang).
Johor DAP chairman Teo Nie Ching said the appointment had been agreed by all three PH component parties: DAP, PKR and Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah).
“DAP proposed Andrew Chen Kah Eng as the Opposition Leader, or Leader of the Balancing Force, in Johor, and the proposal was accepted by our partners from PKR and Amanah,” she told reporters after the Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival at Hutan Bandar Putra here today.
Andrew also held the position during the previous Johor state government’s 2022-2026 term, before the state assembly was dissolved on June 1.
In the 16th Johor state election held on July 11, Barisan Nasional formed the new state government after winning 48 seats, while PH secured eight. — Bernama

Title: Johari Abdul calls for diplomacy to prevent Cambodia-Thailand dispute from straining Asean
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Dialogue and diplomacy must continue to be prioritised in addressing the Cambodia-Thailand border issue to ensure regional peace and stability, said Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul.
He said the approach is important to ensure that bilateral issues do not undermine the spirit of togetherness and unity within Asean, which serves as a platform for member states to build trust, seek common ground and manage differences constructively.
Johari said the border issue was among the matters discussed during his meeting with Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet on the sidelines of the Second Inter-Parliamentary Speakers’ Conference (ISC-2) in Phnom Penh, Cambodia.
“Developments along the Cambodia-Thailand border were also among the matters given attention. Malaysia understands Cambodia’s concerns over the current situation, including its impact on residents in the affected areas.
“In this regard, I stressed that dialogue and diplomacy must always be given space in addressing any differences among Asean member states,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Johari is in the Cambodian capital to attend the conference, jointly hosted by Cambodia’s National Assembly and Senate from August 26 to 28.
He said Malaysia would continue to support efforts to bring all parties back to the negotiating table, with priority given to ensuring that regional peace and stability are preserved.
During the meeting, both sides also exchanged views on strengthening Malaysia-Cambodia ties, covering parliamentary cooperation, the economy, human capital development and youth empowerment.
He said youth from both countries should be given more opportunities to build ties through exchange programmes and participation in the economic, social and inter-parliamentary spheres.
He said the potential to expand cooperation in Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) was also discussed, including via skills training, institutional exchanges and industry collaboration.
At the same time, Johari also expressed appreciation for the Cambodian government’s role in facilitating the operations and investments of Malaysian companies in the country, thereby providing a conducive environment for the Malaysian business community.
He added that Malaysia is committed to continuing close cooperation with Cambodia to strengthen the long-standing bilateral ties for the sake of peace, stability and shared prosperity of the Asean region. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms may offer temporary haze relief as Sarawak braces for prolonged dry spell, says MetMalaysia state director
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 28 — Thunderstorms that have swept parts of Sarawak in recent days may bring temporary relief from the haze, but the improvement is unlikely to last if hot and dry conditions persist and smoke sources remain active, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) Sarawak director Khairul Najib Ibrahim.
He said thunderstorms were a normal occurrence in tropical countries but could develop rapidly when atmospheric conditions became highly unstable.
The combination of intense daytime heat and Sarawak’s naturally high humidity had created conditions conducive to the formation of large convective clouds and localised thunderstorms, some accompanied by strong winds, he told The Borneo Post.
“Thunderstorms in tropical areas can develop very rapidly. A storm may appear relatively normal in the early afternoon but can develop into a storm producing strong winds within two to three hours,” he said.
Khairul Najib said the recent thunderstorms were therefore not necessarily unusual, despite Sarawak experiencing a generally hotter and drier period during the Southwest Monsoon.
He explained that Sarawak typically experienced drier conditions during the Southwest Monsoon, but surface temperatures over the past week had been higher than usual.
“This high daytime heat, combined with Sarawak’s natural humidity, has created highly unstable atmospheric conditions,” he said.
As hot and humid air rises, it forms large storm clouds that can produce thunderstorms and strong winds, he added.
Khairul Najib said haze particles in the atmosphere could also contribute to cloud formation by acting as nuclei around which water droplets could form.
On whether rainfall could disperse the haze, he said heavy rain could improve air quality and visibility by removing some smoke and dust particles from the atmosphere through a process known as wet deposition.
However, he cautioned that the improvement could be short-lived if the sources of smoke remained active.
“If the source of the smoke is still active, for example fires in Kalimantan, the haze can return because south-westerly winds can carry the smoke into Sarawak,” he said.
The explanation comes as Sarawak continues to experience hazy conditions following a prolonged period of hot and dry weather.
Earlier this month, Khairul Najib warned that prevailing winds and hotspots in neighbouring countries could contribute to transboundary haze, particularly in western and southern Sarawak.
Beyond the immediate haze situation and thunderstorms, he said the public should also prepare for the possibility of a prolonged dry spell.
Khairul Najib said Malaysia, including Sarawak, was currently experiencing moderate El Niño conditions, which could continue until at least April 2027.
More significantly, he said the latest projections indicated that the current El Niño could strengthen to a strong or “super” El Niño around October to December this year.
He said such a development could prolong the combination of hot and dry conditions, potentially exacerbating haze if fires and other sources of smoke remained active.
Khairul Najib advised the public to take appropriate precautions, follow instructions from the authorities and keep abreast of weather developments through reliable sources.
He also urged the public to remain vigilant during thunderstorms, which could intensify rapidly under highly unstable atmospheric conditions.
Sarawak had earlier been warned that drier conditions were expected to peak between June and August, coinciding with the Southwest Monsoon and the early influence of El Niño.
Khairul Najib said the current situation highlighted the contrasting weather conditions Sarawak could experience, with sudden thunderstorms occurring alongside a broader pattern of heat and dryness.
“While heavy rain may temporarily wash haze particles from the air, it does not remove the source of the smoke — nor does it signal the end of the underlying dry conditions,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Zetrix AI denies any link to ex-minister Saravanan after graft charges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Zetrix AI Group Bhd has denied any involvement or association with the former Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan following rumours linking the company to the graft charges brought against him today.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said it understood that unfounded rumours or speculation linking it to Saravanan may have contributed to the recent trading activity in its shares.
Zetrix AI ended the day’s trading at 59.5 sen, with 1.05 billion shares traded.
“The company wishes to clarify that it is not implicated in, nor associated in any way whatsoever with, Saravanan, in relation to the three charges of graft brought against him on August 28, 2026 at the Sessions Court concerning the approval of foreign worker quotas,” it said.
The group said there was no basis for the rumours or speculation and that it was not aware of any connection between the charges and the business and affairs of the group.
The company added that, apart from the matters involving the rumours, it was not aware of any other possible explanation for the trading activity.
It also confirmed that it complied with Bursa Malaysia Securities Bhd’s Main Market Listing Requirements, particularly Paragraph 9.03 on immediate disclosure obligations. — Bernama

Title: Power without trust becomes greed, warns Selangor Sultan
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 28 — Sultan of Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah has urged Muslims to shun betrayal of trust, warning that it can erode public confidence and undermine the well-being of society.
In a Facebook post by the Selangor Royal Office, the Ruler said anyone entrusted with managing the assets and interests of the Muslim community, particularly public funds, carries a heavy responsibility before Allah.
His Royal Highness therefore called on everyone to discharge their responsibilities with honesty, no matter how small, saying trust and integrity are fundamental to genuine prosperity and independence.
“Managing public funds with integrity is a sign of our love for the community and the country. Do not allow wealth meant to benefit the people to be misappropriated for personal gain.
“Those guilty must be punished, those who uphold their trust must be supported, and good systems must continue to be improved,” the Ruler said.
Sultan Sharafuddin said true independence also begins with the ability to free oneself from destructive impulses, including greed, temptation and betrayal.
His Royal Highness also expressed concern that while ordinary people struggle with hardship, some continue to enjoy wealth gained through betrayed trust and manipulated justice.
“This is the injustice that arises when power is no longer guided by trust, but driven by greed,” His Royal Highness said.
Sultan Sharafuddin also reminded Muslims that those who commit injustice would not escape divine judgement.
The Ruler warned that signs associated with the end times were becoming increasingly apparent, including responsibilities being placed in the hands of the unqualified and positions of trust being abused for personal gain.
Earlier, Sultan Sharafuddin attended a Yasin recital, prayers and
tahlil
in conjunction with the state-level 69th National Day celebration at the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque.
Raja Muda of Selangor Tengku Amir Shah Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah was also present. — Bernama

Title: SPAN: One dam critical, nine at warning level as El Nino puts pressure on Malaysia’s raw water reserves
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Water levels at 37 of the 49 major dams supplying raw water to Water Treatment Plants (WTPs) in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territory of Labuan remain at normal levels as the country faces the El Nino phenomenon.
The National Water Services Commission (SPAN) said two dams — Jus Dam, Melaka and Labong Dam, Johor — were at the alert level, nine at the warning level and one — Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan — at the critical level.
“Dams at the warning level include Muda Dam and Ahning Dam in Kedah; Upper Layang Dam, Lower Layang Dam, Lebam Dam, Gunung Pulai 1 Dam, Gunung Pulai 2 Dam and Pontian Kechil Dam in Johor, as well as Timah Tasoh Dam in Perlis.
“Timah Tasoh Dam, which had previously remained at the critical level for an extended period, has now improved to the warning level following some rainfall and the pumping of water from the pond into the dam, which helped increase its water storage volume,” the commission said in a statement today.
Overall, all monitored water treatment plants (WTP) were still operating normally but the risk of water supply disruptions could arise if dam levels continued to show a downward trend over time, it added.
SPAN also revealed that the commission, together with the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (PETRA) and all relevant water supply operators, held a meeting on August 26 to assess the raw water situation and coordinate preparedness and mitigation measures, particularly for dams at the alert, warning and critical levels.
The measures being considered are optimising the use of raw water resources, coordinating dam and WTP operations, activating alternative water sources depending on requirements, monitoring water supply demand in high-risk areas, and implementing scheduled water supply if the raw water situation continues to deteriorate.
“In more critical circumstances, restrictions or reductions in water supply to consumers may be considered as a demand management measure, subject to current needs or circumstances and with the minister’s approval in accordance with the applicable legal provisions.
“Such measures will only be considered when other mitigation and resource management measures are no longer sufficient to extend the resilience period of raw water resources,” the commission said.
SPAN said all mitigation measures would be implemented in a targeted manner based on the conditions and level of risk in each area.
It will continue to enhance monitoring and risk assessments based on weather conditions, dam-level trends, the availability of raw water resources and the operational capacity of each WTP. — Bernama

Title: Five-year-old dies in alleged slashing incident in Sibu, police investigate
Article:
SIBU, Aug 28 — Police are investigating the death of a five-year-old child who was allegedly slashed in an incident at Jalan Rantau Panjang Jaya here this afternoon.
The suspect, a man believed to be in his 40s, was reportedly apprehended by a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) team following the incident.
Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad, when contacted, confirmed the case.
“At this point, our men are currently at the crime scene,” he told reporters briefly.
Police have yet to disclose further details, including the circumstances surrounding the incident and the relationship, if any, between the suspect and the victim.
The suspect is believed to be in police custody to assist investigations.
Further details are awaited from police. — The Borneo post

Title: Pahang seeks long-term solution to shallow stretches of Sungai Pahang
Article:
MARAN, Aug 28 — The Pahang government will look into long-term solutions to overcome the problem of the shallow Sungai Pahang in several specific areas, including Kampung Pesagi, here.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government is currently obtaining a complete report from relevant parties on the condition of the river before further action can be decided.
He said the report is important to enable the state government to identify the most suitable methods, including the implementation of short-term, medium-term, and long-term measures to address the issue.
“Right now, I am requesting a report from the district authorities and I will bring it to the exco meeting for us to review, scrutinise and refine for further action,” he said.
He said this when asked by reporters about the issue after attending the inauguration and handover ceremony of the completed pipe replacement project in the Maran district at the Chenor Water Treatment Plant here today.
Wan Rosdy said the state government takes the issue seriously because it affects the economy and activities of residents near the Sungai Pahang, and any actions taken must be based on a comprehensive study to ensure an effective solution.
Meanwhile, Wan Rosdy said the implementation of the pipe replacement programme to address water supply issues and the development of energy infrastructure projects continues to be a priority for the Pahang government in strengthening basic facilities and accelerating the state’s development.
“Four districts have recorded a resolution rate exceeding 90 per cent, while Maran is expected to follow suit in the state government’s efforts to address the water supply issue,” he said.
He said the Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) infrastructure project in Kampung Awah, which involves the construction of a 500kV Transmission Main Intake Substation (PMU), is expected to benefit Pahang by attracting more investors to the state.
It is said that the project involves an allocation of approximately RM350 million and is expected to be completed by 2030.
Wan Rosdy also said that this network will connect strategic locations in the East Coast, thereby building a more robust, resilient energy system ready to support future energy needs.
He added that infrastructure development and the continuous implementation of investment projects are important in boosting the state’s economy, creating job opportunities, and improving the well-being of the people. — Bernama

Title: Mapim to deploy humanitarian mission to Nepal on Sept 5
Article:
IPOH, Aug 28 — The Malaysian Consultative Council of Islamic Organisations (Mapim) will deploy a humanitarian mission to Nepal on September 5 to assist victims affected by massive flash floods in the country.
Mapim president Mohd Azmi Abdul Hamid said the organisation had contacted the Embassy of Nepal to obtain an initial overview of the situation.
“The initial phase of the mission will involve four Mapim volunteers who will assess needs in the affected areas and coordinate the required aid.
“To maximise the impact of the assistance, Mapim is also inviting participation from other local non-governmental organisations (NGOs), including a collaboration with humanitarian organisation MyCare, alongside two local NGOs in Nepal,” he told a press conference on the Regional Mosques Conference 2026 here today.
On August 26, flash floods triggered by an avalanche struck Nepal, leaving at least 469 people dead and more than 1,400 missing, including nearly 540 foreigners.
The incident unleashed a rapid torrent of rocks, ice, mud and debris through Himalayan mountain rivers, sweeping through villages and key infrastructure along a popular trekking route connecting Kathmandu to Lhasa in Tibet.
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported that 57 Malaysians remained untraceable following the incident, based on reports received from family members, friends and employers as of 11pm on August 27.
Commenting on urgent needs on the ground, Mohd Azmi said medical supplies were the top priority, followed by the distribution of basic food packs to victims.
He added that details regarding the special mission would be officially conveyed to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim soon.
“We hope this mission will convey and reflect the solidarity and wish of all Malaysians to come together and help ease the burden faced by the disaster victims there,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘After we shout ‘Merdeka’, don’t leave rubbish everywhere’: SWCorp warns revellers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Corporation (SWCorp) will step up monitoring and enforcement by deploying enforcement personnel at key locations during the National Day celebrations.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said in a statement today that enforcement action would be taken against individuals found committing littering offences in public places throughout the celebrations.
“The public is reminded that littering in public places is an offence that may be subject to action under the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007,” the statement said.
Under the Act, offenders may be fined up to RM2,000 and, upon conviction, ordered to perform up to 12 hours of community service, to be completed within six months.
Community service may include cleaning work such as collecting and sweeping rubbish and cleaning public areas under the supervision of local authorities.
KPKT said visitors are responsible for ensuring that any rubbish they generate is disposed of in the designated bins before leaving the celebration venues.
In the same statement, Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the spirit of National Day should be reflected not only through patriotism but also through discipline and responsibility in keeping the country clean.
“We want Malaysians to turn out in large numbers to celebrate National Day with enthusiasm and pride. After we shout ‘Merdeka’, let us not leave rubbish scattered everywhere.
“Love for the country is not merely about flying the Jalur Gemilang. It is also demonstrated through our attitude towards keeping the country clean and enhancing its image,” he said.
Nga said past experiences, including when Dataran Merdeka was left littered with rubbish after the 2026 World Cup final, should serve as a lesson to prevent a recurrence.
“Cleanliness is not solely the responsibility of cleaning workers. Instead, every individual must take responsibility for the rubbish they generate,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘Why restrain them?’ Anwar says students must be free to speak, think critically
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said young Malaysians should be allowed to speak freely and think critically rather than be controlled.
He said those aged 18 and above were already entitled to vote, so they should be allowed to discuss issues and express their views.
“These children are already 18 years old; they can vote. Why do you want to restrain them? Let them discuss,” he said.
“Will all their views be correct? No. Some may be wrong. But we discuss, we educate them with love. These are our children, our future.”
Anwar was responding to a question from a Form Six student at a meet-and-greet session held at the Teacher Education Institute (IPG) Tuanku Bainun campus, who asked for his advice to youths hoping to enter politics and about the challenges of political life.
He said political decisions shaped national policies, including education policy, and young people should understand that they had a role in discussions affecting their future.
He said he did not agree with the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), which was introduced in the 1970s to restrict university students’ freedom.
“If they hit someone or steal someone’s money, there are laws. But if they give an opinion, listen,” he said.
He said the move to abolish UUCA was intended to give university students room to speak freely and develop creativity, critical judgement and independent views.
“That is why I abolished the Universities and University Colleges Act, which came into force this morning, to give children room to speak freely,” he said.
“I do not want to control them, because I want to educate children with creativity and innovation, with evaluation and critical views.”
Anwar said suppressing students’ views would only weaken society’s ability to judge political claims and public policies.
“Otherwise, it makes the people foolish,” he said.
“We see politicians speaking recklessly, ignorantly and without knowledge. They talk about economics and politics, and just follow people’s sentiments.”
He said political leaders must guide society through facts and knowledge rather than racial or communal sentiment.
“They go to the Malays and incite Malays to hate Indians. Go to the Indians and incite Indians to hate Chinese. We will not get anywhere with this,” he said.
Anwar said young people needed to be encouraged to develop the confidence to hold and express their convictions while learning to assess issues carefully.
“There must be what we always call a courage of conviction,” he said.
“There must be firmness, courage and confidence,” he added.
He said aspiring politicians needed integrity, courage and a genuine desire to defend the public’s interests.
“Why do you want to enter politics? You want to serve your people. You serve your people with integrity,” he said.
“You have to rid the country of excesses of corruption, of abuse of power.”
Anwar said the country needed more intelligent and compassionate people to join politics.
“We need more people like that, because if we leave it, those who will dominate politics are the groups with interests and the corrupt,” he said.
“Good people do not want to [enter politics], so others enter.”
He said leaders should not see public office as a means to gain personal wealth, citing his own decision not to take a salary as prime minister.
“I am not poor. The government provides a car, the government provides an aircraft, the government provides meal allowances,” he said.
“So there is no need to take the salary. Use that salary to help the people.”
He said this was not meant to portray himself as poor, but to show that leadership need not be motivated by money.
“Not everyone who wants to be a leader wants to become rich,” he said.
“Politics is an honourable profession if you make it honourable. It is a dirty, corrupt profession if you are influenced by those who are blatantly corrupt.”
He urged students considering politics to do so out of love for their community and confidence in Malaysia’s future.
“Make sure that you enter politics and work because you love this country and you believe in the future of this country,” he said.

Title: MoH warns against ‘weight-loss pens’ containing unapproved Retatrutide
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has warned the public against buying or using ‘weight-loss pens’ claimed to contain Retatrutide or Reta, as no products containing the drug are registered for use in Malaysia.
In a statement today, MOH said Retatrutide remains an investigational drug currently undergoing Phase 3 clinical trials.
“As of August 17, 2026, no product containing Retatrutide has been registered with the Drug Control Authority (DCA) for use in Malaysia.
“Retatrutide is an investigational medicine undergoing Phase 3 clinical trials and has not received marketing approval from any regulatory authority in the world,” read the statement.
The ministry noted that the online sale of weight loss products was becoming increasingly alarming, including injectable medicines offered directly to the public without examination, prescription or monitoring by registered medical practitioners.
“The use of such products or medicines without proper medical evaluation and monitoring can cause adverse effects and serious complications,” the statement said.
According to MOH, the risks could escalate if adverse effects or complications experienced by users are not identified and treated promptly.
Between January and July this year, the Pharmacy Enforcement Division received 65 complaints and conducted 30 raids related to weight loss products, including 17 raids involving online sales, with total seizures valued at RM477,142.
“Throughout 2026, a total of 209 weight loss product advertisements, including those claiming to contain Retatrutide, were taken down from e-commerce platforms. Additionally, 1,243 advertisements across various media channels were identified, screened and acted upon,” the statement added.
In view of this, MOH advised the public to ensure that weight loss products they intended to purchase were registered and approved for use, and obtained from legitimate sources.
Product registration status can be verified via the “Product Search” function on the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) website, while the authenticity of the FarmaTag hologram can be confirmed using the FarmaChecker feature on the MyUBAT application.
MOH warned that selling unregistered medicines was an offence under the Sale of Drugs Act 1952 [Act 368] and its related regulations, carrying a fine of up to RM50,000 for a first offence and RM100,000 for subsequent offences. — Bernama

Title: ‘I must do something’: Wife of missing Malaysian firefighter flies to Nepal to seek answers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — The wife of a Fire and Rescue Department Special Air Unit officer, who was reported missing in Nepal, flew to Kathmandu today to seek an update on the search for her husband.
Hani Othman said she had decided to travel to Nepal alone to get the latest updates on efforts to find those missing there, saying she did not want to stay at home.
“I decided to take the initiative myself to get an update because I cannot simply stay at home and cry. I must do something.
“I am travelling alone, but I have friends and my husband’s acquaintances there who are ready to help. The Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu has also been informed of my arrival,” she told Bernama when contacted here today.
Hani’s husband, Fire and Rescue Department Senior Fire Officer II Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, in his 40s, better known as Loe, was reported missing during a climbing expedition in Nepal.
Fire and Rescue Department deputy director of the Fire and Rescue Operations Division Mohd Sani Harul was also reported missing during the same climbing expedition.
Hani said her family and close friends had continued to hold special prayers for the safety and wellbeing of her husband and the other missing people.
Before he was reported missing, Mohd Fakhrul Munir shared his personal views on the risks of extreme mountaineering and the impact of the Broad Peak tragedy in a social media post on Aug 2. He also drew a comparison with the 1996 Everest disaster linked to a storm.
Meanwhile, M Vasanthi, 51, said she hoped her sister, M Venilla, 52, another Malaysian who was travelling to Mount Kailash in Tibet, China, when the incident occurred, would be found safe. Venilla has yet to be contacted.
“I am lost for words. I want my sister to return home safely. Her children and I are constantly praying for her safety,” she told Bernama.
Vasanthi said the situation has taken an emotional toll on her sister’s three children, aged 26, 21 and 18, who are now finding it difficult to sleep at night.
“I have decided to stay with them at my sister’s home in Puchong. Although I am struggling to find the strength myself, at a difficult time like this I need to stay strong and be there for them as we get through this difficult period,” she said.
Vasanthi said she last spoke to her sister via video call on Wednesday at about 11.30am Malaysian time, adding that Venilla was on a bus after arriving in Nepal with a group of about 35 friends.
“My sister went there to take part in a religious ceremony and, although she was very tired when we spoke, she seemed happy and even shared views of the beautiful scenery around her from inside the bus,” she said.
The Foreign Ministry said 57 Malaysians remained uncontactable following the major floods that hit Nepal yesterday.
The latest figure was based on information received from family members, friends and employers as of 11pm on August 27. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia step up haze response with weather modification plans
Article:
JAKARTA, Aug 28 — Indonesia has confirmed it is coordinating with Malaysia to tackle transboundary haze, with the first order of business being weather modification operations along border areas.
This comes as smoke from forest and land fires in hard-hit West Kalimantan severely affecting air quality across Sarawak, with Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as high as 195 in some areas as of 9am Friday. An API level of 201 and more is considered very unhealthy.
National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Data, Information, and Disaster Communication Centre Acting Head, Berton Panjaitan, said the two sides are currently discussing wider efforts to address the haze situation.
“On the haze issue, communication with neighbouring countries continues. With Malaysia, bilateral discussions have taken place and we have agreed to strengthen cooperation, including in prevention, monitoring, and support for weather modification operations,” he told Bernama.
Berton said Malaysia had also conveyed its readiness to help in firefighting efforts.
Jakarta had yet to make an official request for direct firefighting assets such as water-bombing support. However, he noted that the government remains open to cooperation when the need arises and in accordance with existing mechanisms.
Malaysia and Indonesia had on August 24 agreed to intensify prevention and firefighting measures to address transboundary haze, following discussions between Malaysian Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup and Indonesian Environment Minister Jumhur Hidayat.
Arthur said Indonesia had also granted permission for Malaysia to enter its airspace to conduct cloud-seeding operations.
The haze is also affecting Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Penang, Kedah, and Perak which have recorded unhealthy air quality readings.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Consulate in Pontianak said the haze situation in Kalimantan has worsened this year after no severe haze was reported in 2024 and 2025.
“The haze has worsened today. We comply with all directives issued by the local authorities, including wearing masks, shifting school lessons online, and reducing movement or outdoor activities except when necessary,” the consulate told Bernama.
The consulate said its focus is on the health of the 577 Malaysians registered in West Kalimantan, most of whom reside across Kalimantan as expatriates.
Malaysia has supported local firefighting efforts before. In 2023, the consulate contributed six water pumps to the West Kalimantan Governor’s Office. — Bernama

Title: Teacher charged with 10 counts of sexually assaulting pupils in Mukah
Article:
MUKAH, Aug 28 — A 56-year-old teacher has been charged in the Mukah Magistrate’s Court today with 10 counts of sexually assaulting female pupils between 2022 and 2024.
Mukah police chief DSP Muhamad Rizal Alias said the accused, who was a teacher at a primary school here at the time of the alleged offences, was accused of committing the offences against 10 girls while in a position of trust as their teacher.
“The alleged offences took place in the school’s science laboratory and classrooms,” he said in a statement.
Rizal said a police report was lodged by a secondary school counselling teacher in Mukah on August 7 after receiving a complaint from one of the alleged victims.
“Following the report, a team from the Mukah District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Division arrested the teacher for investigation and further action,” he said.
The accused was charged under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16(1) of the same Act.
If convicted under Section 14(a), he faces up to 20 years’ imprisonment and whipping. Section 16(1) provides for an additional maximum five-year jail term and at least two strokes of whipping.
The accused, who was represented by a lawyer, did not enter a plea.
The court granted bail of RM2,000 for each charge, totalling RM20,000, with two local sureties. The accused has since paid the bail.
The case will be mentioned again on October 20. — The Borneo Post

Title: Anwar: Budget 2027 to include allowance for Form Six students
Article:
SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will be including an allowance for Form Six students under Budget 2027, which is due to be tabled in October.
He said the government decided this after feedback from pre-university students who noted that there was no government allowance for those in Form Six.
“From Year One until Form Five, there are allowances. There are allowances at university level. But Form Six and pre-university students do not have them,” he said at the IPG Tuanku Bainun campus here today.
“So in our Budget this October, I will include an allocation and allowance for Form Six students,” he said.
However, Anwar did not disclose the amount of the allowance or details on eligibility and implementation.
“We will need to look into our financial capacity before announcing the amount we plan to approve,” he explained.
The prime minister said education continued to receive the largest allocation under the Madani government’s federal budgets because it was central to the country’s future.
However, he acknowledged that resources remained insufficient despite the higher allocation.
“Is it enough? Not yet. But every ministry and department says the same thing — it is still not enough,” he said.
Anwar said access to quality education must continue to be expanded and made available for students from all backgrounds, including those from poor urban and rural families, villages, estates and remote areas.
He said Malaysia’s success would be measured by whether children from disadvantaged communities could access opportunities to become professionals, educators, civil servants and specialists in fields such as artificial intelligence and the semiconductor industry.

Title: Anwar tells schools, varsities: Zero tolerance for bullying, arrogance
Article:
SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged schools and higher education institutions to show zero tolerance towards bullying as such behaviour could undermine the country’s future.
He said students who bully others because they are stronger, more capable or come from better circumstances must not be allowed to thrive in the education system.
“There must be no compromise. Once we start compromising, the country and its future will not be destroyed,” he said in his speech at IPG Tuanku Bainun campus here.
Anwar said academic achievement alone could not build a civilised nation without values, character and respect for others.
He said Malaysia must pursue new knowledge, including information technology and artificial intelligence, while preserving “adab” (good manners) and ethical conduct.
“We want knowledge and character. We do not want a country that reaches for the sky in technology while its human values are eroded,” he said.
The prime minister said students who bully, belittle or humiliate others could not be allowed to become future leaders.
“If a Form Five student is already bullying others, or a Form Six student is arrogant, imagine what sort of leader he will become tomorrow. The country will be ruined,” he said.
Anwar also urged teachers and lecturers to act firmly against such behaviour.
He said isolated cases should not define an entire school, but they should not be trivialised either.
“Sometimes a school has 1,000 students and only four are involved in serious bullying. The media reports on the four, not the hundreds doing well.
“But that does not mean we should take it lightly. We must build a new culture,” he said.
He added that the spirit of independence must include freedom of thought and the rejection of prejudice based on race, skin colour, culture or religion.

Title: MetMalaysia: Haze expected to persist across Sarawak tomorrow, with thunderstorms in several areas
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 28 — Haze is expected to persist across all divisions in Sarawak tomorrow (August 29), with isolated thunderstorms and rain forecast in several areas, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
The department’s weather forecast said haze is expected statewide in the morning, affecting Sri Aman, Betong, Bintulu, Kapit, Kuching, Miri, Mukah, Samarahan, Sarikei, Serian, Sibu and Limbang.
In the afternoon, thunderstorms are forecast in a few places in Kuching, Kapit, Miri and Limbang, while haze is expected to continue in Sri Aman, Betong, Bintulu, Mukah, Samarahan, Sarikei, Serian and Sibu.
At night, rain is expected in a few places in Kuching, Kapit, Miri and Limbang, while haze is forecast to persist in the remaining divisions.
“Temperatures statewide are expected to range between 24° and 35°Celsius,” MetMalaysia forecasted.
For coastal Sarawak waters, winds over the western part of the state are forecast to blow from the west-south-west at 10 to 20km/h, with wave heights ranging from 0.5 to 1.0 metres.
Northern Sarawak waters are expected to experience west-north-westerly winds at 10 to 20km/h, with wave heights also ranging from 0.5 to 1.0 metres. — The Borneo Post

Title: In Sarawak, Jalan Lapangan Terbang junction to close overnight for works from Aug 28 to 29
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 28 — The junction from Jalan Lapangan Terbang to Lorong Lapangan Terbang 1, near the voco hotel, will be temporarily closed overnight from Friday at 10pm until Saturday at 5am for sheet-piling dismantling works.
Sarawak Metro Sdn Bhd, in a statement on Friday, advised road users to use alternative routes and plan their journeys accordingly during the closure.
“Please adhere to all traffic management control measures, road warning signs and speed limits, to ensure the safety of road users and construction workers,” it said.
Sarawak Metro said the public would be notified should there be any changes to the temporary closure.
For enquiries, the public may contact the KUTS hotline at 1300-88-5887 from 8am to 5pm, Monday to Friday, except public holidays, or email 555999@sarawak.gov.my or info@mysarawakmetro.com. — The Borneo Post pic
Alternative route to Lorong Lapangan Terbang 1. — The Borneo Post pic

Title: Anwar: Malaysia coordinating aid to Nepal, may deploy Smart elite rescuers
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Aug 28 — Malaysia is coordinating the delivery of aid to Nepal following the devastating floods in the country, including the possibility of deploying the Malaysian Special Search and Rescue Team (Smart), said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The prime minister said the National Security Council (MKN) was in close contact with the Nepalese government to determine the appropriate form of assistance, whether financial aid or the deployment of rescue personnel.
“At the moment, MKN is coordinating whether we should send the Smart team or aid, which we will decide,” he told reporters after Friday prayers at Masjid Sembilang here today.
Anwar said several countries, including India, China and Bangladesh, had also provided assistance following the disaster, which he described as occurring on an unprecedented scale.
He said the Foreign Ministry was obtaining the latest list of Malaysians in the affected areas, while efforts to ascertain their status were ongoing.
Anwar also urged the families of Malaysians in the affected areas to contact the Foreign Ministry through the channels provided to facilitate efforts to obtain the latest information.
Yesterday, the Prime Minister instructed all relevant departments, including MKN, and the Foreign Ministry, to immediately identify and contact Malaysians affected by the disaster.
Earlier, the Foreign Ministry said 57 Malaysians remained uncontactable following yesterday’s floods at the Nepal-Tibet border areas.
The latest figure was based on reports received from family members, friends and employers as of 11 pm on Aug 27. — Bernama

Title: Odd-job worker, cook each jailed 10 years, caned two strokes for sexually assaulting teen girl in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 28 — The Sessions Court has sentenced a 22-year-old oddjobber and a 20-year-old cook to 10 years in prison and six strokes of the cane each for sexually assaulting a teenage girl.
Oddjobber Daniel Arrazy Salmi Abdullah also received an additional three-year prison term for possessing child sexual abuse material.
Judge Musli Ab Hamid convicted both men on their own guilty pleas to the charge under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017 (SOACA), which provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years and caning upon conviction.
Daniel committed the offence against the 16-year-old at a house in Simunjan Bazaar at around 1am on May 20, while the cook, who is an Indonesian national, sexually assaulted the same girl in a hostel room in Serian at around 9.30am early this month.
According to the facts of the case, the cook, who is the victim’s colleague, groped the teenager before pulling her into a hostel room, where he sexually assaulted her.
She tried to break free but was unable to.
Following the incident, she lodged a police report, which led to the cook’s arrest on August 16.
Investigations also led to the arrest of the oddjobber that same night to assist with investigations into the sexual assault case.
Further investigations revealed that the same victim had been sexually assaulted in two separate incidents, each involving a different accused.
During a search of the oddjobber’s smartphone, police also found nine videos containing child sexual abuse material.
He was subsequently charged under Section 10 of the Act in the same courtroom, where he also pleaded guilty.
Judge Musli ruled that Daniel’s three-year sentence for this charge would run consecutively with the 10-year sentence imposed for the sexual assault offence.
Deputy public prosecutor Adriana Maisarah Mohd Farid appeared for the prosecution, while both Daniel and the foreign cook were unrepresented by counsel.
The case was investigated by Insp Victor Buckand Dusim Oh. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sri Aman records Sarawak’s worst air quality at 4pm as API hits 215
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 28 — Sri Aman recorded Sarawak’s worst air quality today, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 215 at 4pm, placing the district in the very unhealthy category.
The reading, recorded by the Air Pollutant Index of Malaysia (APIMS), was the highest among monitoring stations across the state, with Sri Aman the only area in Sarawak to record an API reading above 200.
IPD Serian recorded the second-highest reading at 182, followed by Sarikei at 163 and Kuching at 160, all in the unhealthy category.
Sibu recorded an API reading of 151, Bintulu 136, Miri 99 and Samalaju 99, while ILP Miri recorded 87, Mukah 87, Limbang 72 and Kapit 71.
No reading was available for Samarahan.
The Department of Environment (DOE), in its haze and air quality status report issued today, said air quality nationwide had deteriorated, with several areas in the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak recording unhealthy API readings due to haze moving from various directions.
According to the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC), 514 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan and 176 in Sumatra on Aug 27, while three hotspots were detected in Malaysia, including one in Sarawak.
The regional haze map issued today also showed moderate to thick haze over western Borneo, with several monitoring stations in western Sarawak recording unhealthy to hazardous readings.
DOE said it had increased enforcement activities and daily patrols in areas potentially affected by open burning, while the National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan had been activated to coordinate the government agencies’ response.
The department also advised the public to monitor the latest hourly API readings and avoid open burning.
Under the National Haze Action Plan, schools, kindergartens and nurseries are to be closed immediately when the API exceeds 200. — The Borneo Post

Title: Sarawak’s Long Banga, Ba Kelalan STOLports to be upgraded this year with RM30m allocation
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 28 — Work to upgrade the Long Banga and Ba Kelalan STOLports is expected to begin this year following the federal government’s approval of RM30 million for the two rural air facilities.
Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah said RM15 million had been allocated for each STOLport under the Airport Development Fund.
“We have just approved the allocation and, Insya-Allah, we want to start something this year.
“There is still design work and other preparations to be done,” he told reporters after launching the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme here on Friday.
He said the upgrades would include terminal improvements and, where feasible, runway extensions based on site conditions.
“We want our rural STOLports to also have a new look and be upgraded according to current needs,” he said.
Hasbi said longer runways would enable the facilities to handle more passengers, noting that due to runway length Twin Otter flights are limited to nine passengers.
He said the federal government is also upgrading airports in Sabah and Sarawak, including Miri Airport, where the project is currently at the design stage and involves more than RM400 million.
The combined allocation for airport upgrading projects in Sabah and Sarawak exceeds RM1 billion, covering Tawau, Lahad Datu, Kota Kinabalu, and Sandakan airports in Sabah.
Meanwhile, Hasbi said the proposed new Lawas Airport was under the Sarawak government through the Northern Region Development Authority (NRDA), with site preparation underway in Sundar.
On Bebuling STOLport, he said he had yet to receive information on its planned landing test.
“That is under the state, so I have not received any information on the landing test yet. I will find out,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: LSH Infra-Pertama Makmur JV win job for Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan elevated highway project
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 28 — LSH Infra Sdn Bhd and Pertama Makmur Sdn Bhd Joint Venture has been awarded the proposed development of the Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Elevated Highway (BSE), a strategic infrastructure project aimed at strengthening connectivity and easing traffic congestion in Greater Kuala Lumpur.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the Cabinet had agreed in principle to the proposed development of the BSE, reflecting the MADANI Government’s commitment to providing high-impact infrastructure that benefits the people, stimulates economic growth and enhances the country’s competitiveness in a sustainable manner.
He said the BSE, envisaged as a high-capacity connecting route, would integrate several major highway networks to improve connectivity across Greater Kuala Lumpur.
“This includes the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, Maju Expressway (MEX), Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), New Pantai Expressway (NPE), Shah Alam Expressway (KESAS) and the Kuala Lumpur Traffic Dispersal System (SPRINT) network.
“The development of the elevated highway along this strategic alignment has the potential to provide an alternative route for road users and facilitate movement between the northern, southern and east coast corridors of Peninsular Malaysia,” he told Bernama today.
The project is to be undertaken by LSH Infra and Pertama Makmur Joint Venture, with both companies bringing experience in construction and infrastructure-related projects.
LSH Infra is a subsidiary of Lim Seong Hai Capital Bhd, an investment holding company principally involved through its subsidiaries in construction and construction-related services and solutions, building materials, lighting and mechanical and electrical products and services, machinery rental, property development and facilities management.
Lim Seong Hai Capital was incorporated in Malaysia on Nov 11, 2020 under the Companies Act 2016 and was listed on Bursa Malaysia’s LEAP Market on July 30, 2021 before subsequently transferring to the ACE Market on March 21, 2025.
Its construction-related business is supported by subsidiaries involved in building materials, construction and construction-related services, hardware and tools, machinery rental, property development and investment holding.
Pertama Makmur, meanwhile, is a bumiputera-owned company incorporated in 1986. The company is a CIDB G7 contractor and is registered as a contractor with the Ministry of Finance (MOF), Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), FGV Holdings Bhd and Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor).
It has completed more than 50 projects to date, with a cumulative contract value exceeding RM1.4 billion.
Among its major completed projects are the Sungai Kerayong Flood Mitigation Project under the River of Life programme, construction of an elevated interchange at the Jalan Pudu-Jalan Imbi-Jalan Hang Tuah intersection in Kuala Lumpur, upgrading of Jalan Semarak from Jalan Tun Razak to the DUKE Highway, construction of the sewerage pipeline network in Melaka and the Damansara-Shah Alam Elevated Expressway (DASH) Package CB4.
Pertama Makmur currently has five projects in hand with a total contract value of about RM500 million.
The major projects include Central Spine Road (CSR) Package 4C, the Sungai Pendang Flood Mitigation Project, and the widening and upgrading of Jalan Yew and Jalan Sungai Besi in Kuala Lumpur.
Yesterday, Nanta was reported as saying that the better connectivity would enhance public mobility, improve logistics efficiency and facilitate the movement of goods, while also potentially reducing travel time and improving access to employment centres, educational institutions and public services.
He said the BSE was not merely a new highway project but also a long-term investment in strengthening connectivity, inclusive development and the country’s economic competitiveness in line with the aspirations of Malaysia MADANI.
Following the approval in principle, the Works Ministry (KKR), together with relevant agencies including the Public Private Partnership Unit (UKAS), will continue negotiations and detailed assessments to finalise the project’s implementation structure.
“The government will ensure that every aspect of the project is assessed comprehensively, particularly in terms of public interest, value for money for the country and fiscal sustainability, before any final decision on its implementation is made,” he said.
The minister added that the proposed development of the BSE would adopt a private-sector financing approach, ensuring that its implementation would not involve direct financial commitments from the Federal Government.
Nanta said the government would also examine selected proposals for other infrastructure solutions to complement the existing road network and address traffic congestion in the Klang Valley.
He said the proposals would be considered based on strategic needs, capacity enhancement and their impact on traffic flow.
“KKR will continue to ensure that the subsequent process is carried out carefully, transparently and based on the interests of the people and country, in line with the government’s commitment to developing a more efficient, integrated and sustainable transport system to support economic growth and improve the people’s quality of life,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Upside-down Jalur Gemilang, Perak flag: Perak MCA apologises, staff quits
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 28 — Perak MCA has apologised to the Sultan of Perak and Malaysians over the upside-down display of the Jalur Gemilang and Perak flag at its state headquarters in Ipoh, which went viral on social media today.
Perak MCA state liaison committee chairman Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said the party took full responsibility and viewed the incident seriously, Kosmo! Online reported.
He said the unintentional mistake was rectified immediately, while the staff member involved had resigned with immediate effect.
“The incident occurred this morning when an elderly staff member at the Perak MCA state headquarters was tasked with installing and putting up the Jalur Gemilang and Perak flag to mark National Month.
“Perak MCA stresses that this was an unintentional mistake and there was absolutely no intention to insult the Jalur Gemilang or the Perak state flag,” he said here today.
Mah said both flags were taken down immediately and put up correctly once the error was noticed.
He also confirmed that police officers from the Ipoh police station visited the MCA headquarters at about 1pm to investigate and record statements from the staff member involved and the headquarters’ administrative officer.
“Perak MCA has and will continue to give full cooperation to the police.
“The staff member expressed regret over the incident and voluntarily offered to resign,” he said.
Mah said the Perak MCA headquarters accepted the resignation out of respect for the staff member’s personal decision.
“He has served with dedication for many years. We will manage matters concerning him in relation to this incident appropriately,” he said.

Title: ‘We have to accept whatever comes’: Family of Bomba special forces officer missing in Nepal stays positive
Article:
SIK, Aug 28 — The family of Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, 44, a member of the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department’s (JBPM) special forces team, who remains missing following the flash floods and landslide in Rasuwa, Nepal, is holding onto hope that he and his companions will be found safe.
His brother, Mohd Saiful Munir Mohd Isa, 46, said the family is choosing to stay positive and believes the communication blackout is due to the disaster that has struck the area.
He said the family has not stopped praying that the professional climber, better known as Loe, and his group will be located soon.
“But we also have to accept whatever comes, even if things take a turn for the worse,” he told reporters today.
Mohd Saiful Munir said the family does not see Loe’s trip to Nepal as unusual, given that his brother is deeply passionate about climbing and frequently travels abroad for climbing activities.
“You could say Nepal is like his second home… he goes there about three to five times a year,” he said, adding that Loe is also an avid cyclist.
Mohd Saiful Munir, who is an operations officer at the Port Klang Fire and Rescue Station, said the last time he spoke to Loe was about a week ago, before he departed for Nepal.
Based on the group’s planned route, he said they were likely in the valley area when the disaster struck.
“We’re treating this as a disaster where he’s essentially trapped and unable to reach out,” he said, adding that he will only rely on official information from the authorities.
Yesterday, media reported that two JBPM officers were among the Malaysians still uncontactable following the flash floods in Rasuwa, Nepal.
JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad identified them as Planning and Research Division deputy director Mohd Sani Harul and Central Region Academy officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa.
The two officers are part of a group of 10 Malaysians on their way to Everest Base Camp. — Bernama
